Such notification shall contain the details of a contact point where more information can be obtained, a description of the nature of the breach (including, where possible, categories and approximate number of data subjects and personal data records concerned), its likely consequences and the measures taken or proposed to address the data breach, including measures to mitigate its possible adverse effects. Where, and in so far as, it is not possible to provide all information at the same time, the initial notification shall contain the information then available and further information shall, as it becomes available, subsequently be provided without undue delay.

(d) The data importer shall cooperate with and assist the data exporter to enable the data exporter to comply with its obligations under Regulation (EU) 2016/679, in particular to notify its controller so that the latter may in turn notify the competent supervisory authority and the affected data subjects, considering the nature of processing and the information available to the data importer.

8.7. Sensitive data

Where the transfer involves personal data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, or trade union membership, genetic data, or biometric data for the purpose of uniquely identifying a natural person, data concerning health or a person's sex life or sexual orientation, or data relating to criminal convictions and offences (hereinafter 'sensitive data'), the data importer shall apply the specific restrictions and/or additional safeguards set out in Schedule B.

8.8. Onward transfers

The data importer shall only disclose the personal data to a third party on documented instructions from the controller, as communicated to the data importer by the data exporter. In addition, the data may only be disclosed to a third party located outside the European Union (in the same country as the data importer or in another third country, hereinafter 'onward transfer') if the third party is or agrees to be bound by these Clauses, under the appropriate Module, or if: (i) the onward transfer is to a country benefitting from an adequacy decision pursuant to Article 45 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 that covers the onward transfer; (ii) the third party otherwise ensures appropriate safeguards pursuant to Articles 46 or 47 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679; (iii) the onward transfer is necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims in the context of specific administrative, regulatory or judicial proceedings; or (iv) the onward transfer is necessary in order to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another natural person.

Any onward transfer is subject to compliance by the data importer with all the other safeguards under these Clauses, in particular purpose limitation.

8.9. Documentation and compliance (a)

The data importer shall promptly and adequately deal with enquiries from the data exporter or the controller that relate to the processing under these Clauses.

(b) The Parties shall be able to demonstrate compliance with these Clauses. In particular, the data importer shall keep appropriate documentation on the processing activities carried out on behalf of the controller.

(c) The data importer shall make all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations set out in these Clauses available to the data exporter, which shall provide it to the controller.

(d) The data importer shall allow for and contribute to audits by the data exporter of the processing activities covered by these Clauses, at reasonable intervals or if there are indications of non-compliance. The same shall apply where the data exporter requests an audit on instructions of the controller. In deciding on an audit, the data exporter may consider relevant certifications held by the data importer.

3.

(e) Where the audit is carried out on the instructions of the controller, the data exporter shall make the results available to the controller.

(f) The data exporter may choose to conduct the audit by itself or mandate an independent auditor. Audits may include inspections at the premises or physical facilities of the data importer and shall, where appropriate, be carried out with reasonable notice.

(g) The Parties shall make the information referred to in paragraphs (b) and (c), including the results of any audits, available to the competent supervisory authority on request.

MODULE FOUR: Transfer processor to controller

8.1. Instructions (a) The data exporter shall process the personal data only on documented instructions from the data importer acting as its controller. (b) The data exporter shall immediately inform the data importer if it is unable to follow those instructions, including if such instructions infringe Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or other Union or Member State data protection law. (c) The data importer shall refrain from any action that would prevent the data exporter from fulfilling its obligations under Regulation (EU) 2016/679, including in the context of sub-processing or as regards cooperation with competent supervisory authorities.

(d) After the end of the provision of the processing services, the data exporter shall, at the choice of the data importer, delete all personal data processed on behalf of the data importer and certify to the data importer that it has done so, or return to the data importer all personal data processed on its behalf and delete existing copies.

8.2. Security of processing (a)

The Parties shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to ensure the security of the data, including during transmission, and protection against a breach of security leading to accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure or access (hereinafter 'personal data breach').

In assessing the appropriate level of security, they shall take due account of the state of the art, the costs of implementation, the nature of the personal data, the nature, scope, context and purpose(s) of processing and the risks involved in the processing for the data subjects, and in particular consider having recourse to encryption or pseudonymisation, including during transmission, where the purpose of processing can be fulfilled in that manner.

(b) The data exporter shall assist the data importer in ensuring appropriate security of the data in accordance with paragraph (a). In case of a personal data breach concerning the personal data processed by the data exporter under these Clauses, the data exporter shall notify the data importer without undue delay after becoming aware of it and assist the data importer in addressing the breach.

(c) The data exporter shall ensure that persons authorised to process the personal data have committed themselves to confidentiality or are under an appropriate statutory obligation of confidentiality.

8.3. Documentation and compliance (a)

The Parties shall be able to demonstrate compliance with these Clauses.

(b) The data exporter shall make available to the data importer all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with its obligations under these Clauses and allow for and contribute to audits.

6.3. Precedence and Interpretation.

In the event of any inconsistency between this Agreement and the text of Clause 8 above, the SCC Clause 8 prevails, as mandated by Article 46 GDPR and the Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914.

6.4.

Integration with Neurodata-Specific Requirements.

The obligations in Clause 8 shall apply in conjunction with: Where these impose stricter safeguards than the SCCs, the stricter safeguard applies.

6.5. Module-Specific Application.

The applicable SCC Module (Module 1, 2, 3, or 4) shall be selected for each Exporter-Importer relationship in Schedule A, and the Module-specific text above applies accordingly.

ARTICLE 6A -AI AND ALGORITHMIC PROCESSING OF NEURODATA

ARTICLE 6A -AI AND ALGORITHMIC PROCESSING OF NEURODATA 6A.1.1.

6A.1. Scope of AI Processing

Neurodata or Governed Artefacts may be used to train, fine-tune, validate, benchmark, query or operate an AI system only where the activity is expressly described in Schedules A and B, legally and institutionally authorised, and subject to the safeguards identified under Annexures 1-3.

6A.1.2.

AI Systems trained on Neurodata shall remain subject to governance obligations where Functional Exposure persists, irrespective of whether direct identifiers remain present. 6A.2. Permitted Inference and Prohibited Use No inference, profiling, reconstruction, prediction or decision-making activity may be undertaken unless it: The Parties shall identify prohibited inferences and uses, including any restrictions relating to behavioural manipulation, employment, insurance, commercial scoring, law enforcement, discriminatory decision-making or unrelated mental-state inference.

6A.3. Model Governance and Documentation

The Data Importer shall maintain complete documentation describing: • model architecture, training data sources, and parameters • preprocessing steps applied to neurodata • model evaluation metrics, bias testing, and explainability measures • any third-party AI services or cloud-based training tools used Documentation must be provided to the Data Exporter upon request.

6A.4.1. Prohibition on Unauthorised Model Training Neurodata may not be used for training or fine-tuning AI Systems unless: • expressly permitted under the purposes of processing, • supported by a valid lawful basis under Article 10, • described in Annex I.B, and • approved by the Data Exporter. 6A.4.2. AI-based processing is not prohibited per se. Such processing may proceed where authorised under this Agreement and subject to the applicable Risk Tier determined under Annexure 1 and recorded in Schedule B, any transfer or access conditions identified under the Neurodata Transfer and Access Decision Tool in Annexure 2 and recorded in Schedule C, and any derivative or model-governance requirements identified under Annexure 3.6A.5. AI Explainability and Human Oversight 6A.5.1. Where Neurodata contributes to model outputs used to inform research conclusions, clinical hypotheses or participant-level interpretations, the Data Importer shall ensure human oversight proportionate to the applicable Risk Tier and Functional Exposure. Persons exercising oversight shall have the competence, information and authority necessary to assess the outputs, recognise their limitations and intervene where appropriate. 6A.5.2. As a contractual safeguard, the Data Importer shall not use Neurodata or Governed Artefacts to make decisions based solely on automated processing that produce legal or similarly significant effects concerning a Data Subject unless expressly authorised in writing by the Data Exporter and permitted under applicable law and any binding transfer instrument. Before such use, the Data Importer shall document the applicable legal grounds, any additional conditions governing special-category or sensitive data, and the safeguards implemented. The Data Exporter's authorisation shall not substitute for any legally required consent, approval or other condition. 6A.5.3. For any automated decision authorised under Article 6A.5.2, the Data Importer shall, where necessary in cooperation with the Data Exporter, provide affected Data Subjects with intelligible information about the decision, its basis and likely consequences, and effective means to make representations, contest the decision and obtain meaningful human review.

6A.5.4. On request, the Data Importer shall provide the Data Exporter with clear explanations of relevant model outputs, their material limitations and the oversight measures applied. These contractual safeguards supplement applicable law and binding transfer instruments and shall not be interpreted as reducing their protections.

6A.6. Protection Against Inference and Reconstruction Attacks

The Data Importer must implement technical safeguards against: • model inversion, 3.

• membership inference, • re-identification through latent spaces, • extraction of sensitive cognitive states from trained models.

6A.7. Governance of Derivative and Model-Associated Artefacts

Features, embeddings, synthetic outputs, model weights and other computational artefacts generated using Neurodata shall be assessed under Annexures 1 and 3. Their technical form or incorporation into an AI system does not automatically determine Tier 5 status. Where continuing Functional Exposure is identified, the artefact shall remain subject to the safeguards and contractual modules applicable to the resulting tier.

6A.8. Cross-Border Replication and Cloud Requirements AI Systems or training pipelines may not: • replicate data or model artefacts outside approved locations, • rely on cloud services that automatically distribute data globally, • utilise GPU clusters in non-approved jurisdictions.

6A.9. Audit Rights The Data Exporter may audit AI Systems using transferred neurodata and may require suspension of any model development that threatens data subjects' mental privacy or autonomy.

Article 6B -Continuity Protection

6B.1.

The Parties acknowledge that governance obligations may become fragmented as Neurodata or Governed Artefacts move across jurisdictions, institutions, repositories, cloud infrastructures, AI systems and downstream-use environments.

6B.2. The Parties shall implement and maintain the safeguards required for the applicable Risk Tier throughout the authorised lifecycle of the Neurodata or Governed Artefact.

6B.3.

Removal of identifiers or technical transformation shall not, by itself, terminate governance obligations where Functional Exposure persists.

6B.4. Tier assignment is informed by Functional Exposure, while statutory classification and legal status remain determined under Applicable Law.

6B.5. Repository-specific and controlled-access requirements shall be recorded in Schedule D and implemented in accordance with Annexure 5.

6B.6. Upstream governance conditions. Before processing or sharing an object derived from externally obtained Neurodata, the Parties shall identify and comply with upstream conditions applicable to that object or activity. A lower Risk Tier does not displace such conditions. The MDTAA shall not be interpreted as granting permissions withheld by an upstream instrument or as authorising the Parties to amend that instrument. Where permission is unclear, the affected activity shall not proceed until the uncertainty has been resolved.

ARTICLE 7 -DATA PROVENANCE AND LAWFUL SOURCE

7.1. Compatibility with SCC Clause 8.1 and 8.2.

Data Exporters shall ensure that all Personal Data and Neurodata shared under this Agreement originate from lawful, transparent, and ethically approved sources, in full alignment with the transparency, purpose limitation, and accuracy obligations contained in SCC Clause 8.1, 8.2, and 8.3.

7.2. Provenance Documentation.

The Data Exporter shall maintain a proportionate, traceable provenance record identifying the source dataset and version, source institution or repository, documented collection and sharing authorisations or institutional attestations, applicable consent and ethics conditions, upstream access instruments and approvals, and the transformations producing the object shared under this Agreement.

Upstream documentation may be incorporated by stable, versioned reference where it provides sufficient evidence and remains available for authorised review. Confidential source documents need not be duplicated or disclosed without authority; appropriate attestations or controlled-access references may be used. The Data Exporter shall document the basis for the proposed downstream use and release, and identify material gaps or uncertainties requiring resolution before proceeding.

The record shall be available to authorised reviewers and, where incorporated and applicable, in accordance with SCC Clause 8.9.

7.3. Limitations on Downstream Use.

Data Importers may only process Personal Data for the purposes identified in Schedule B and consistent with SCC Clause 8, unless an exception listed in Clause 8.1 applies.

7.4. Functional Exposure Principle

Governance obligations under this Agreement shall be determined not solely by legal classification or identifiability, but also by the continuing Functional Exposure associated with the Neurodata or Governed Artefact.

7.5. Openly Available Sources.

Public availability or an open licence shall not, by itself, establish that every proposed use, linkage, inference, transformation or onward release is authorised. The Data Exporter shall record the dataset version and licence or dedication, applicable legal restrictions, and documented consent, ethics, institutional and repository conditions relevant to the proposed activity. The assessment shall distinguish binding legal or contractual restrictions from ethical commitments and institutional requirements; original study conditions shall not automatically be treated as contractual obligations of a downstream user without an applicable basis. Material uncertainty concerning authorisation shall be referred for appropriate review before the affected activity proceeds. The following text is therefore incorporated verbatim. The data importer shall not sub-contract any of its processing activities performed on behalf of the data exporter under these Clauses to a sub-processor without the data exporter's prior specific written authorisation. The data importer shall submit the request for specific authorisation at least [Specify time period] prior to the engagement of the sub-processor, together with the information necessary to enable the data exporter to decide on the authorisation. The list of sub-processors already authorised by the data exporter can be found in Annex III. The Parties shall keep Annex III up to date.

ARTICLE 8 -USE OF SUB-PROCESSORS AND ONWARD PROCESSING

OPTION 2: GENERAL WRITTEN AUTHORISATION

The data importer has the data exporter's general authorisation for the engagement of sub-processor(s) from an agreed list. The data importer shall specifically inform the data exporter in writing of any intended changes to that list through the addition or replacement of sub-processors at least [Specify time period] in advance, thereby giving the data exporter sufficient time to be able to object to such changes prior to the engagement of the sub-processor(s). The data importer shall provide the data exporter with the information necessary to enable the data exporter to exercise its right to object.

(b) Where the data importer engages a sub-processor to carry out specific processing activities (on behalf of the data exporter), it shall do so by way of a written contract that provides for, in substance, the same data protection obligations as those binding the data importer under these Clauses, including in terms of third-party beneficiary rights for data subjects. The Parties agree that, by complying with this Clause, the data importer fulfils its obligations under Clause 8.8. The data importer shall ensure that the sub-processor complies with the obligations to which the data importer is subject pursuant to these Clauses.

(c) The data importer shall provide, at the data exporter's request, a copy of such a sub-processor agreement and any subsequent amendments to the data exporter. To the extent necessary to protect business secrets or other confidential information, including personal data, the data importer may redact the text of the agreement prior to sharing a copy.

(d) The data importer shall remain fully responsible to the data exporter for the performance of the sub-processor's obligations under its contract with the data importer. The data importer shall notify the data exporter of any failure by the sub-processor to fulfil its obligations under that contract.

(e) The data importer shall agree a third-party beneficiary clause with the sub-processor whereby -in the event the data importer has factually disappeared, ceased to exist in law or has become insolvent -the data exporter shall have the right to terminate the sub-processor contract and to instruct the sub-processor to erase or return the personal data. The data importer has the controller's general authorisation for the engagement of sub-processor(s) from an agreed list. The data importer shall provide the controller with the information necessary to enable the controller to exercise its right to object. The data importer shall inform the data exporter of the engagement of the sub-processor(s).

MODULE THREE: Transfer processor to processor

(b) Where the data importer engages a sub-processor to carry out specific processing activities (on behalf of the controller), it shall do so by way of a written contract that provides for, in substance, the same data protection obligations as those binding the data importer under these Clauses, including in terms of third-party beneficiary rights for data subjects. The Parties agree that, by complying with this Clause, the data importer fulfils its obligations under Clause 8.8. The data importer shall ensure that the sub-processor complies with the obligations to which the data importer is subject pursuant to these Clauses.

(c) The data importer shall provide, at the data exporter's or controller's request, a copy of such a sub-processor agreement and any subsequent amendments. To the extent necessary to protect business secrets or other confidential information, including personal data, the data importer may redact the text of the agreement prior to sharing a copy.

(d) The data importer shall remain fully responsible to the data exporter for the performance of the sub-processor's obligations under its contract with the data importer. The data importer shall notify the data exporter of any failure by the sub-processor to fulfil its obligations under that contract.

(e) The data importer shall agree a third-party beneficiary clause with the sub-processor whereby -in the event the data importer has factually disappeared, ceased to exist in law or has become insolvent -the data exporter shall have the right to terminate the sub-processor contract and to instruct the sub-processor to erase or return the personal data.

Approved Sub-Processors shall be recorded in the MDTAA Supplementary Sub-Processor Register. Where SCC Annex III is required under the selected Module and authorisation option, it shall also be completed and maintained in the official SCC Appendix. Where general written authorisation applies, the agreed list and changes to it shall be managed in accordance with the applicable Clause 9 requirements.

8.5. Precedence

In case of conflict between this Article and any other provision relating to subcontracting, SCC Clause 9 prevails.

ARTICLE 9 -ETHICS APPROVAL AND OVERSIGHT

9.1. Ethics Compliance.

All Transfers and subsequent processing must comply with applicable ethical review requirements and research governance standards. This obligation supplements but does not limit SCC Clause 8.1.

9.2. Ongoing Oversight.

Ethics approvals must cover: (a) international transfer risks under Clause 14 SCC, (b) protections for vulnerable populations, (c) neurodata-specific dignity, autonomy, and mental privacy protections.

9.3. Reports and Notifications.

Where ethics approval conditions affect processing, Data Importers shall be notified, consistent with SCC Clause 8.2 (transparency obligations). 3.10A.1.2. The Tiered Neurodata Risk Classification Framework set out in Annexure 1 establishes a structured mechanism for classifying Neurodata according to the degree of participant traceability, inferential capacity, reconstructability, and downstream governance risk. 10A.1.3. The Neurodata Governance Decision Tool set out in Annexure 1 provides the operational workflow through which Neurodata and Governed Artefacts shall be assessed and assigned to the appropriate Risk Tier. 10A.2. Initial Risk Classification 10A.2.1. Prior to transfer, access, processing, repository deposit, AI use, or other authorised activity under this Agreement, all Neurodata and Governed Artefacts shall be classified in accordance with Annexure 1.10A.2.2. The applicable Risk Tier shall be recorded in Schedule B (Neurodata Profile and Transfer Summary). 10A.2.3. Where an assessment under the Neurodata Transfer and Access Decision Tool is required under Article 13A, the applicable Risk Tier shall also be reflected in Schedule C. 10A.3. Governance Consequences of Risk Classification 10A.3.1. The assigned Risk Tier establishes the applicable baseline safeguards. The Required Safeguards for the particular object and activity shall be identified under Annexure 1 and, where applicable, Annexure 2, taking account of linkage status, the relevant actors, the access or release model, and applicable legal, ethical, institutional, repository, and approval conditions. Any alternative safeguard package permitted for public release shall be documented under Annexure 1 §3.2 and Annexure 2 Step 8B. 10A.3.2. Risk classification shall be interpreted in conjunction with the tier-specific safeguards contained in Annexure 1, any transfer-or access-specific safeguards identified under Annexure 2, and any additional repository or controlled-access requirements contained in Schedule D and Annexure 5.10A.4. Ongoing Review of Risk Classification 10A.4.1. Risk classification shall not be treated as a one-time labelling exercise. 10A.4.2. The assigned Risk Tier shall be reviewed whenever Neurodata: (a) are linked to other datasets; (b) undergo technical transformation; (c) are transferred to a new recipient, repository, or jurisdiction; (d) are reused for a materially different purpose; (e) become incorporated into computational systems; (f) are used for AI training, fine-tuning, embedding generation, predictive modelling, or related activities; or (g) are otherwise subjected to material changes capable of altering Functional Exposure. 10A.4.3. Where reassessment results in a change to the applicable Risk Tier, Schedule B and any affected provisions of this Agreement shall be updated accordingly. 10A.5. Functional Exposure Principle 10A.5.1. Risk Tier assignment under this Agreement shall be informed by identifiability, traceability, inferential capacity, reconstruction potential, linkage, technical persistence and other forms of Functional Exposure. 10A.5.2. Removal of direct identifiers or technical transformation does not automatically reduce the applicable tier. 10A.5.3. A Risk Tier is a governance classification. It is provisional only where the relevant assessment record identifies it as provisional or specialist review is pending. It does not determine the object's statutory classification or legal status under Applicable Law. 10A.5.4. Where relevant information is incomplete, the provisional classification and the measures required to resolve the uncertainty shall be recorded in Schedule B and, where a transfer or access pathway is being assessed, Schedule C. ARTICLE 10B -NEURAL DERIVATIVE AND EMBEDDING GOVERNANCE DECISION TOOL 10B.1. Purpose The Derivative and Embedding Governance Decision Tool in Annexure 3 establishes a post-transformation assessment mechanism for determining whether technical transformation has altered the Functional Exposure of Neurodata or a Governed Artefact. 10B.2. Application The Tool shall be completed where Neurodata undergo, or are proposed to undergo: (a) feature extraction or dimensionality reduction; (b) embedding or latent-representation generation; (c) dataset linkage; (d) predictive modelling, classification, profiling or reconstruction; (e) synthetic-data generation; (f) AI training, fine-tuning, validation or benchmarking; (g) federated learning or model updating; or (h) incorporation into persistent computational infrastructure. 10B.3. Assessment requirements The assessment shall consider: (a) the nature, purpose and method of transformation; (b) provenance and version history; (c) independent circulation or deployment; (d) participant or group linkage; (e) inference, prediction, profiling and reconstruction; (f) memorisation, extraction, inversion and membership inference; (g) persistence within models or infrastructure; (h) access and deployment conditions; (i) retention and decommissioning; and (j) deletion or technically feasible model unlearning. 10B.4. Outcomes The Tool shall produce one of the following outcomes: (a) retain the existing tier; (b) refer for Tier 4 classification or reassessment; (c) confirm Tier 5 classification; (d) specialist review required; or (e) do not proceed where the identified exposure cannot be governed.

ARTICLE 10 -LAWFUL BASIS, CONSENT, AND WITHDRAWAL

10B.5. Tier 5 Tier 5 shall be confirmed only where the completed assessment demonstrates that neural information persists within a model or computational infrastructure in a manner capable of creating continuing Functional Exposure. Model incorporation alone does not establish Tier 5 status. Where incorporation is known but continuing exposure remains materially uncertain, Tier 5 safeguards shall apply provisionally pending specialist review.

10B.6. Reassessment

Where Annexure 3 identifies a material change in Functional Exposure, Annexure 1 shall be reapplied. Where the artefact is transferred, remotely accessed, hosted, deposited or deployed externally, Annexure 2 shall also be completed or updated.

10B.7. Legal status

An outcome under Annexure 3 does not determine the legal status of the transformed artefact. Applicable legal classification remains determined under Applicable Law.

ARTICLE 11 -DATA SUBJECT RIGHTS

11.1. General 11.1.1. The Parties shall ensure that Data Subjects can effectively exercise their rights under applicable data protection law, including but not limited to the rights of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, objection, data portability, and rights related to automated decision-making. 11.1.2. These rights shall be exercised in a manner that is fully consistent with the obligations set out in the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) incorporated into this Agreement, in particular Clause 10 (Data subject rights), which is set out verbatim below.

11.2. Integration of EU SCC Clause 10 (Verbatim Text)

For Transfers subject to the SCCs pursuant to Articles 3, 5 and 6 of this Agreement, the Parties agree that Clause 10 of Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914 of 4 June 2021 applies in full. The text of Clause 10 is incorporated verbatim as follows:

Clause 10 -Data subject rights MODULE ONE: Transfer controller to controller (a) The data importer, where relevant with the assistance of the data exporter, shall deal with any enquiries and requests it receives from a data subject relating to the processing of his/her personal data and the exercise of his/her rights under these Clauses without undue delay and at the latest within one month of the receipt of the enquiry or request. The data importer shall take appropriate measures to facilitate such enquiries, requests and the exercise of data subject rights.

Any information provided to the data subject shall be in an intelligible and easily accessible form, using clear and plain language.

(b) In particular, upon request by the data subject the data importer shall, free of charge: (i) provide confirmation to the data subject as to whether personal data concerning him/her is being processed and, where this is the case, a copy of the data relating to him/her and the information in Annex I; if personal data has been or will be onward transferred, provide information on recipients or categories of recipients (as appropriate with a view to providing meaningful information) to which the personal data has been or will be onward transferred, the purpose of such onward transfers and their ground pursuant to Clause 8.7; and provide information on the right to lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority in accordance with Clause 12(c)(i); (ii) rectify inaccurate or incomplete data concerning the data subject; (iii) erase personal data concerning the data subject if such data is being or has been processed in violation of any of these Clauses ensuring third-party beneficiary rights, or if the data subject withdraws the consent on which the processing is based.

(c) Where the data importer processes the personal data for direct marketing purposes, it shall cease processing for such purposes if the data subject objects to it.

(d) The data importer shall not make a decision based solely on the automated processing of the personal data transferred (hereinafter 'automated decision'), which would produce legal effects concerning the data subject or similarly significantly affect him/her, unless with the explicit consent of the data subject or if authorised to do so under the laws of the country of destination, provided that such laws lays down suitable measures to safeguard the data subject's rights and legitimate interests. In this case, the data importer shall, where necessary in cooperation with the data exporter: (i) inform the data subject about the envisaged automated decision, the envisaged consequences and the logic involved; and (ii) implement suitable safeguards, at least by enabling the data subject to contest the decision, express his/her point of view and obtain review by a human being.

+(e) Where requests from a data subject are excessive, in particular because of their repetitive character, the data importer may either charge a reasonable fee taking into account the administrative costs of granting the request or refuse to act on the request.

(f) The data importer may refuse a data subject's request if such refusal is allowed under the laws of the country of destination and is necessary and proportionate in a democratic society to protect one of the objectives listed in Article 23 (1) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679.

(g) If the data importer intends to refuse a data subject's request, it shall inform the data subject of the reasons for the refusal and the possibility of lodging a complaint with the competent supervisory authority and/or seeking judicial redress.

MODULE TWO: Transfer controller to processor

(a) The data importer shall promptly notify the data exporter of any request it has received from a data subject. It shall not respond to that request itself unless it has been authorised to do so by the data exporter.

3.

(b) The data importer shall assist the data exporter in fulfilling its obligations to respond to data subjects' requests for the exercise of their rights under Regulation (EU) 2016/679. In this regard, the Parties shall set out in Annex II the appropriate technical and organisational measures, considering the nature of the processing, by which the assistance shall be provided, as well as the scope and the extent of the assistance required.

(c) In fulfilling its obligations under paragraphs (a) and (b), the data importer shall comply with the instructions from the data exporter.

MODULE THREE: Transfer processor to processor

(a) The data importer shall promptly notify the data exporter and, where appropriate, the controller of any request it has received from a data subject, without responding to that request unless it has been authorised to do so by the controller.

(b) The data importer shall assist, where appropriate in cooperation with the data exporter, the controller in fulfilling its obligations to respond to data subjects' requests for the exercise of their rights under Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or Regulation (EU) 2018/1725, as applicable. In this regard, the Parties shall set out in Annex II the appropriate technical and organisational measures, considering the nature of the processing, by which the assistance shall be provided, as well as the scope and the extent of the assistance required.

(c) In fulfilling its obligations under paragraphs (a) and (b), the data importer shall comply with the instructions from the controller, as communicated by the data exporter.

MODULE FOUR: Transfer processor to controller

The Parties shall assist each other in responding to enquiries and requests made by data subjects under the local law applicable to the data importer or, for data processing by the data exporter in the EU, under Regulation (EU) 2016/679.

It shall deal promptly with any complaints it receives from a data subject. [OPTION: The data importer agrees that data subjects may also lodge a complaint with an independent dispute resolution body at no cost to the data subject. It shall inform the data subjects, in the manner set out in paragraph (a), of such redress mechanism and that they are not required to use it or follow a particular sequence in seeking redress.] MODULE ONE: Transfer controller to controller MODULE TWO: Transfer controller to processor MODULE THREE: Transfer processor to processor (b) In case of a dispute between a data subject and one of the Parties as regards compliance with these Clauses, that Party shall use its best efforts to resolve the issue amicably in a timely fashion. The Parties shall keep each other informed about such disputes and, where appropriate, cooperate in resolving them. (c) Where the data subject invokes a third-party beneficiary right pursuant to Clause 3, the data importer shall accept the decision of the data subject to: (i) lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority in the Member State of his/her habitual residence or place of work, or the competent supervisory authority pursuant to Clause 13; (ii) refer the dispute to the competent courts within the meaning of Clause 18. Neurodata-Specific Redress Requirements (Complementary to SCC Clause 11)

In addition to the SCC obligations above, the Parties agree to the following sector-specific adaptations for neurodata: (a) Enhanced Transparency for Neurodata The Data Importer shall ensure that the information required in Clause 11(a) includes an explanation, written in clear, accessible, non-technical language, of: • the nature of neural signals processed; • any inferences that may be drawn from neural data; • the risks associated with re-identification or mental state inference; • the procedure for contesting such inferences.

(b) Special Handling of Neurodata-Related Complaints The Data Importer shall designate at least one individual trained in neuroethics or neural data governance to handle complaints relating to: • neural data interpretation; • cognitive or affective inference; • algorithmic decision-making involving neurodata.

(c) Timeliness Complaints relating to neural data that involve algorithmic inferences impacting autonomy, identity, or mental privacy must be addressed within 20 days, unless a shorter period is required by law.

(d) Documentation The Data Importer must document: • the nature of each complaint, • all steps taken to investigate it, and • its resolution, and shall make this documentation available to the Data Exporter and the competent supervisory authority upon request.

This Article shall be read together with: In the event of any conflict, the SCC text incorporated verbatim shall prevail to the extent required by law. 11B.4. Where complete removal is not technically feasible, the responsible Party shall document the residual influence, restrict further use and access, implement available mitigation, consider isolation or decommissioning, and maintain continuing governance for as long as Functional Exposure persists. 11B.5. Completion of deletion, return, mitigation or unlearning measures shall be documented and certified in accordance with the Return, Deletion and Certification Module and, where applicable, the Persistent Artefact, Model Retention and Unlearning Module.

ARTICLE 12 -LOCAL LAWS, GOVERNMENT ACCESS & TRANSFER IMPACT ASSESSMENTS

12.1. General Principle

The Parties acknowledge that international transfers are subject to the requirements set out in Clause 14 of the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs). The following text is therefore incorporated verbatim into this Agreement and forms an integral and mandatory part of all Data Transfers made under this MDTA.

12.2. EU SCC Clause 14 (Verbatim Text) Clause 14 -Local laws and practices affecting compliance with the Clauses MODULE ONE: Transfer controller to controller MODULE TWO: Transfer controller to processor MODULE THREE: Transfer processor to processor MODULE FOUR: Transfer processor to controller (where the EU processor combines the personal data received from the third country-controller with personal data collected by the processor in the EU)

The Parties warrant that they have no reason to believe that the laws and practices in the third country of destination applicable to the processing of the personal data by the data importer, including any requirements to disclose personal data or measures authorising access by public authorities, prevent the data importer from fulfilling its obligations under these Clauses. This is based on the understanding that laws and practices that respect the essence of the fundamental rights and freedoms and do not exceed what is necessary and proportionate in a democratic society to safeguard one of the objectives listed in Article 23(1) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679, are not in contradiction with these Clauses.

(b) The Parties declare that in providing the warranty in paragraph (a), they have taken due account in particular of the following elements: (i) the specific circumstances of the transfer, including the length of the processing chain, the number of actors involved and the transmission channels used; intended onward transfers; the type of recipient; the purpose of processing; the categories and format of the transferred personal data; the economic sector in which the transfer occurs; the storage location of the data transferred; (ii) the laws and practices of the third country of destination, including those requiring the disclosure of data to public authorities or authorising access by such authorities, relevant in light of the specific circumstances of the transfer, and the applicable limitations and safeguards; (iii) any relevant contractual, technical or organisational safeguards put in place to supplement the safeguards under these Clauses, including measures applied during transmission and to the processing of the personal data in the country of destination.

(c) The data importer warrants that, in carrying out the assessment under paragraph (b), it has made its best efforts to provide the data exporter with relevant information and agrees that it will continue to cooperate with the data exporter in ensuring compliance with these Clauses.

(d) The Parties agree to document the assessment under paragraph (b) and make it available to the competent supervisory authority on request.

3.

(e) The data importer agrees to notify the data exporter promptly if, after having agreed to these Clauses and for the duration of the contract, it has reason to believe that it is or has become subject to laws or practices not in line with the requirements under paragraph (a), including following a change in the laws of the third country or a measure (such as a disclosure request) indicating an application of such laws in practice that is not in line with the requirements in paragraph (a).

[For Module Three: The data exporter shall forward the notification to the controller.] (f) Following a notification pursuant to paragraph (e), or if the data exporter otherwisehas reason to believe that the data importer can no longer fulfil its obligations under these Clauses, the data exporter shall promptly identify appropriate measures (e.g. technical or organisational measures to ensure security and confidentiality) to be adopted by the data exporter and/or data importer to address the situation [for Module Three: if appropriate in consultation with the controller].

The data exporter shall suspend the data transfer if it considers that no appropriate safeguards for such transfer can be ensured, or if instructed by [for Module Three: the controller or] the competent supervisory authority to do so. In this case, the data exporter shall be entitled to terminate the contract, insofar as it concerns the processing of personal data under these Clauses. If the contract involves more than two Parties, the data exporter may exercise this right to termination only with respect to the relevant Party, unless the Parties have agreed otherwise. Where the contract is terminated pursuant to this Clause, Clause 16(d) and (e) shall apply.

12.5. Precedence of SCC Clause 14

Where any provision of this Agreement conflicts with Clause 14 SCC, Clause 14 shall prevail to the extent necessary to guarantee an essentially equivalent level of protection for Data Subjects.

ARTICLE 12A -SUPERVISORY AUTHORITY

12A.1. Competent Supervisory Authority

For purposes of this Agreement and the incorporated EU Standard Contractual Clauses, the competent supervisory authority shall be determined in accordance with SCC Clause 13, which is incorporated verbatim below: SCC CLAUSE 13 (VERBATIM TEXT) 3.

Clause 13 -Supervision MODULE ONE: Transfer controller to controller MODULE TWO: Transfer controller to processor MODULE THREE: Transfer processor to processor (a) [Where the data exporter is established in an EU Member State:] The supervisory authority with responsibility for ensuring compliance by the data exporter with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 as regards the data transfer, as indicated in Annex I.C, shall act as competent supervisory authority. [Where the data exporter is not established in an EU Member State, but falls within the territorial scope of application of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 in accordance with its Article 3(2) and has appointed a representative pursuant to Article 27(1) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679:] The supervisory authority of the Member State in which the representative within the meaning of Article 27(1) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 is established, as indicated in Annex I.C, shall act as competent supervisory authority. [Where the data exporter is not established in an EU Member State, but falls within the territorial scope of application of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 in accordance with its Article 3(2) without however having to appoint a representative pursuant to Article 27(2) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679:] The supervisory authority of one of the Member States in which the data subjects whose personal data is transferred under these Clauses in relation to the offering of goods or services to them, or whose behaviour is monitored, are located, as indicated in Annex I.C, shall act as competent supervisory authority.

The data importer agrees to submit itself to the jurisdiction of and cooperate with the competent supervisory authority in any procedures aimed at ensuring compliance with these Clauses. In particular, the data importer agrees to respond to enquiries, submit to audits and comply with the measures adopted by the supervisory authority, including remedial and compensatory measures. It shall provide the supervisory authority with written confirmation that the necessary actions have been taken.

12A.2. Neurodata-Specific Obligation to Cooperate

In addition to the obligations above, the Data Importer shall: (a) provide, where required, additional documentation regarding neural data processing, including: • signal acquisition specifications; • data model architectures; • inference logic or explainability reports; • risk assessments relating to cognitive inference.

(b) permit the competent supervisory authority to examine: • data minimisation controls; • pseudonymisation techniques for neurodata; • any cross-border model training involving neural datasets.

(c) ensure any request by a supervisory authority relating to neurodata is answered in writing within 15 days or a shorter period if legally required.

(d) The data importer agrees to preserve the information pursuant to paragraphs (a) to (c) for the duration of the contract and make it available to the competent supervisory authority on request.

(e) Paragraphs (a) to (c) are without prejudice to the obligation of the data importer pursuant to Clause 14(e) and Clause 16 to inform the data exporter promptly where it is unable to comply with these Clauses.

15.2.

Review of legality and data minimisation (a)

The data importer agrees to review the legality of the request for disclosure, in particular whether it remains within the powers granted to the requesting public authority, and to challenge the request if, after careful assessment, it concludes that there are reasonable grounds to consider that the request is unlawful under the laws of the country of destination, applicable obligations under international law and principles of international comity. The data importer shall, under the same conditions, pursue possibilities of appeal. When challenging a request, the data importer shall seek interim measures with a view to suspending the effects of the request until the competent judicial authority has decided on its merits. It shall not disclose the personal data requested until required to do so under the applicable procedural rules. These requirements are without prejudice to the obligations of the data importer under Clause 14(e).

(b) The data importer agrees to document its legal assessment and any challenge to the request for disclosure and, to the extent permissible under the laws of the country of destination, make the documentation available to the data exporter. It shall also make it available to the competent supervisory authority on request.

[For Module Three: The data exporter shall make the assessment available to the controller.] (c) The data importer agrees to provide the minimum amount of information permissible when responding to a request for disclosure, based on a reasonable interpretation of the request.

13.3. Additional Neurodata-Specific Safeguards

In addition to SCC Clause 15, the Data Importer must: 12.3.1. Notify the Data Exporter immediately if a public authority attempts to access: • raw neural recordings; • neural signatures or identifiers; • models trained on neurodata; • inferred mental states, cognitive profiles, or behavioural predictions.

13.3.2. Implement the safeguards described in:

• Annex II (TOMs), • Annex IV (Cybersecurity and Neurodata Risk Framework).

13.3.3.

Ensure that any compelled disclosure complies with the data minimisation principle and avoids revealing: • re-identification keys; • data schemas or model architecture enabling reverse engineering; • cross-participant identifiers.

13.4. Precedence

Where any MDTA provision conflicts with SCC Clause 15, SCC Clause 15 prevails to guarantee an essentially equivalent level of protection under Article 44 of the GDPR.

Where transformation, derivative generation, synthetic-data generation or AI/model incorporation is proposed, Annexure 3 shall be completed. Any resulting change in tier or safeguards shall be incorporated into the Neuro-TADT.

13A.7. Outcomes

The Neuro-TADT shall produce one of four outcomes: (a) Proceed, where all requirements and safeguards are in place; (b) Proceed after supplementary safeguards are implemented, where specified safeguards must be implemented and verified before commencement; (c) Redesign the transfer or access pathway, where the current pathway cannot maintain the Required Safeguards but may become governable through material modification; or (d) Do not proceed, where the pathway is unauthorised or identified exposure cannot be governed adequately.

13A.8. Recording and reassessment

The outcome, reasons, conditions, responsible Parties, implementation deadlines and verification measures shall be recorded in Schedule C. The Neuro-TADT shall be repeated following a Material Change. ARTICLE 15 -NON-COMPLIANCE AND TERMINATION

The Parties agree that the following text of Clause 16 of the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (2021) is incorporated verbatim and applies in full to all transfers of Personal Data and Neurodata governed by this Agreement: SCC CLAUSE 16 (VERBATIM TEXT) (a)

Clause 16 -Non-compliance with the Clauses and termination

The data importer shall promptly inform the data exporter if it is unable to comply with these Clauses, for whatever reason.

In the event that the data importer is in breach of these Clauses or unable to comply with these Clauses, the data exporter shall suspend the transfer of personal data to the data importer until compliance is again ensured or the contract is terminated. This is without prejudice to Clause 14(f).

(c) The data exporter shall be entitled to terminate the contract, insofar as it concerns the processing of personal data under these Clauses, where: (i) the data exporter has suspended the transfer of personal data to the data importer pursuant to paragraph (b) and compliance with these Clauses is not restored within a reasonable time and in any event within one month of suspension; (ii) the data importer is in substantial or persistent breach of these Clauses; or (iii) the data importer fails to comply with a binding decision of a competent court or supervisory authority regarding its obligations under these Clauses.

In these cases, it shall inform the competent supervisory authority [for Module Three: and the controller] of such non-compliance. Where the contract involves more than two Parties, the data exporter may exercise this right to termination only with respect to the relevant Party, unless the Parties have agreed otherwise. Personal data that has been transferred prior to the termination of the contract pursuant to paragraph (c) shall at the choice of the data exporter immediately be returned to the data exporter or deleted in its entirety. The same shall apply to any copies of the data.

[For Module Four:] Personal data collected by the data exporter in the EU that has been transferred prior to the termination of the contract pursuant to paragraph (c) shall immediately be deleted in its entirety, including any copy thereof.

The data importer shall certify the deletion of the data to the data exporter. Until the data is deleted or returned, the data importer shall continue to ensure compliance with these Clauses.

In case of local laws applicable to the data importer that prohibit the return or deletion of the transferred personal data, the data importer warrants that it will continue to ensure compliance with these Clauses and will only process the data to the extent and for as long as required under that local law.

(e) Either Party may revoke its agreement to be bound by these Clauses where (i) the European Commission adopts a decision pursuant to Article 45(3) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 that covers the transfer of personal data to which these Clauses apply; or (ii) Regulation (EU) 2016/679 becomes part of the legal framework of the country to which the personal data is transferred.

This is without prejudice to other obligations applying to the processing in question under Regulation (EU) 2016/679.

15.1 Neurodata-Specific Extensions (Complementary to SCC Clause 16)

The following additional requirements apply specifically to Neurodata and are in addition to the verbatim SCC text: (a) Suspension for Mental Privacy Risk The Data Exporter must suspend transfers immediately if the Data Importer's processing of Neurodata: • poses a risk of unintended inference (e.g., emotional state, cognitive workload, pathology detection), • exceeds the stated purpose (Annex I.B), or • introduces new algorithmic models not documented in Annex II.

(c) Termination for Unauthorised Neurodata Inference Persistent or substantial violations include: • creation of unauthorised neural profiles; • re-identification attempts; • cross-linking neural data with behavioural or biometric datasets; • use of Neurodata in generative models without explicit lawful basis.

(d) Deletion Protocols for Neural Signals and Derivatives Upon termination: • raw neural signals, • processed signal features, • trained model weights derived from Neurodata, and • embeddings or latent representations must be deleted or returned, unless the applicable Module requires deletion only.

(e) Certification Requirements The Data Importer's deletion certification must include: • code repositories scrubbed of datasets; • model retraining or model-masking logs; • confirmation of erasure from backups; • documentary proof of secure destruction.

15.2 Relationship to Other Articles

Article 15 must be read together with:

Article 12 (Local Laws & Schrems II Assessment -Clause 14) • Article 13 (Government Access Requests -Clause 15) • Article 14 (Liability -Clause 12) If any inconsistency exists, the SCC text (above) prevails. The Parties agree that this shall be the law of _______ (specify Member State).] [OPTION 2 (for Modules Two and Three): These Clauses shall be governed by the law of the EU Member State in which the data exporter is established. 16.1. Completion of Chosen Governing Law

The Parties must complete the appropriate option in Annex I.C depending on the Module(s) selected under Article 5 of this Agreement.

If more than one Module applies, each transfer pathway must specify its corresponding governing law.

ARTICLE 17 -FORUM AND JURISDICTION

The Parties agree that the following text of Clause 18 of the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (2021) is incorporated verbatim into this Agreement: SCC CLAUSE 18 (VERBATIM TEXT) Clause 18 -Choice of forum and jurisdiction MODULE ONE: Transfer controller to controller MODULE TWO: Transfer controller to processor MODULE THREE: Transfer processor to processor (a) Any dispute arising from these Clauses shall be resolved by the courts of an EU Member State. (b) The Parties agree that those shall be the courts of ____________ (specify Member State). (c) A data subject may also bring legal proceedings against the data exporter and/or data importer before the courts of the Member State in which he/she has his/her habitual residence.

(d) The Parties agree to submit themselves to the jurisdiction of such courts.

MODULE FOUR: Transfer processor to controller

Any dispute arising from these Clauses shall be resolved by the courts of ________________ (specify country).

17.1. Neurodata-Specific Jurisdiction Considerations (Complementary)

Given the risks associated with neural signal interpretation, mental privacy, and algorithmic inference, the Parties additionally agree: (a)

The Data Importer must maintain a legal contact point for neurodata-related complaints, regulatory inquiries, or proceedings within the selected jurisdiction.

(b) Any additional project-specific jurisdiction, forum, dispute-resolution mechanism or institutional contact point shall be identified in Schedule A, subject to Applicable Law and without limiting any forum, remedy or third-party beneficiary right available under an applicable SCC Module.

(c) Nothing in this Agreement limits data subjects' rights to bring claims under Article 80 GDPR using nonprofit representation.

17.2. Relationship With Other Articles

This Article must be read alongside: • Article 11A (Redress -SCC Clause 11), • Article 12A (Supervision -SCC Clause 13), • Article 14 (Liability -SCC Clause 12), • Article 15 (Non-Compliance -SCC Clause 16).

Where conflict exists, the SCC text prevails.

ARTICLE 18 -INTERPRETATION, HIERARCHY, AND RESOLUTION OF INCONSISTENCIES

18.1. Purpose

The Parties acknowledge that this Agreement consists of multiple interrelated governance instruments, including the Main Agreement, Schedules, Annexures, and incorporated Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs). This Article establishes the hierarchy applicable to the interpretation of those instruments and the resolution of any inconsistency between them.

18.2.

Principles of Interpretation 18.2.1. This Agreement shall be interpreted as a coherent governance framework intended to preserve continuity of protection throughout the lifecycle of Neurodata, including collection, processing, transfer, access, storage, transformation, AI use, repository deposit, downstream reuse, and dissemination.

18.2.2.

To the extent reasonably possible, all provisions of this Agreement shall be interpreted harmoniously and in a manner that gives effect to the objectives set out in Article 3.

18.2.3.

The Parties shall interpret governance obligations according to the principle of Functional Exposure, recognising that governance obligations may continue to apply even where Neurodata have been transformed, pseudonymised, embedded, modelled, or otherwise altered.

18.3. Hierarchy of Instruments

In the event of any inconsistency, conflict, ambiguity, duplication, or overlap between provisions contained in this Agreement, the following hierarchy shall apply in descending order of authority: (a) Applicable Law, including mandatory constitutional, statutory, regulatory, ethics, health-information, privacy, cybersecurity, binding conditions of any applicable statutory access authorisation or data permit, and data-protection requirements applicable to the relevant Parties or processing activities;

Neuro-Transfer and Access Decision Outcomes

Where Schedule C imposes supplementary safeguards, restrictions, conditions, review requirements, transfer limitations, repository conditions, or governance controls arising from a Neuro-TADT assessment, those requirements shall prevail over any inconsistent provision contained in Schedule A, Schedule B, or any Annexure, unless prohibited by applicable law or the SCCs.

18.5. Repository Governance Conditions

Where Schedule D imposes repository-specific or DAC-specific governance conditions, those conditions shall prevail over any inconsistent provision contained in Schedule A, Schedule B, or the Annexures, provided that such conditions remain consistent with the Main Agreement, applicable law, and the SCCs.

18.6. Annexures as Governance Instruments

The Annexures form an integral part of this Agreement and provide interpretive, methodological, operational, and governance guidance for implementation of the Parties' obligations. Unless expressly stated otherwise, the Annexures shall not be interpreted as limiting obligations imposed by the Main Agreement, Schedule C, Schedule D, applicable law, or the SCCs. 18.7.

Most Protective Interpretation

Where two or more provisions appear applicable to the same Neurodata, Governed Artefact, transfer pathway, repository environment, or processing activity, the provision that provides the higher level of protection for Data Subjects, participants, communities, or affected populations shall apply, provided that such interpretation remains consistent with applicable law.

18.8. No Reduction of Protection

No Schedule, Annexure, repository condition, institutional policy, contractual arrangement, technical control, or governance mechanism implemented under this Agreement shall be interpreted as reducing the level of protection otherwise required by applicable law, the SCCs, or the Main Agreement.

18.9.

Digital Governance and Automated Implementation

The Parties acknowledge that this Agreement may be implemented through digital governance platforms, including automated compliance and contract-management systems. Where this Agreement is operationalised through such systems, the hierarchy established in this Article shall govern the resolution of conflicting rules, workflows, safeguards, or automated compliance determinations.

ARTICLE 19 -VERSION CONTROL

The Parties acknowledge that this Agreement may exist in digitally generated or dynamically updated versions. Version histories shall be maintained, and the most recently executed version shall govern unless otherwise agreed.

CERTIFICATION Repository Representative Name: Title: Institution: Signature: ANNEXURE 1 TIERED NEURODATA RISK CLASSIFICATION FRAMEWORK AND NEURODATA GOVERNANCE DECISION TOOL 1. PURPOSE AND STATUS 1.1. This Annexure establishes: (a) the Tiered Neurodata Risk Classification Framework applicable under the Modular Neurodata Transfer and Access Agreement ("MDTAA"); and (b) the Neurodata Governance Decision Tool through which Neurodata and Neurodata-derived objects shall be assigned to an appropriate Neurodata Risk Tier. 1.2. The purpose of this Annexure is to enable the Parties, researchers, repository managers, Data Access Committees, ethics committees, data stewards and other authorised governance bodies to: (a) classify Neurodata according to its current technical form and Functional Exposure; (b) identify the highest applicable Neurodata Risk Tier; (c) determine the minimum governance measures required before storage, access, sharing, transfer, transformation, reuse or AI deployment; and (d) identify whether further assessment is required under the other MDTAA governance tools. 1.3. This Annexure forms an integral part of the MDTAA and shall be applied before any Neurodata or Governed Artefact is: (a) transferred or made accessible to another Party; (b) deposited in or accessed through a repository; (c) processed within a cloud, secure computing or distributed computational environment; (d) transformed into a derivative representation; (e) used to train, fine-tune, validate, benchmark or deploy an AI or machine-learning system; or (f) reused for a materially different purpose.

1.4.

The classification assigned under this Annexure does not determine whether the relevant processing, access or transfer is legally authorised under Applicable Law. It identifies the minimum governance measures required to preserve Continuity of Protection in addition to all applicable legal, ethical, institutional, contractual and repository requirements.

2. GOVERNING PRINCIPLES

>GOVERNING PRINCIPLES

2.1. Functional Exposure

Neurodata shall be classified according to its Functional Exposure, meaning the capacity of a Neurodata object, irrespective of its technical transformation, identifiability status or statutory classification, to: (a) identify or trace an individual or group; (b) support an inference concerning neurological, cognitive, emotional or behavioural states; (c) enable reconstruction, profiling, prediction or classification; (d) reveal information concerning health, disability, vulnerability, mental state, identity or behaviour; or (e) preserve neural information within an AI model or persistent computational system.

Ordinary aggregate or cohort-level statistical description that satisfies the Tier 1 criteria does not constitute Functional Exposure solely because it describes neurological, cognitive or behavioural characteristics at group level. Group-level Functional Exposure refers to information capable of supporting materially consequential inference, profiling, prediction, classification or other governance-relevant effects concerning a sufficiently defined group or population.

2.2. Technical transformation does not end governance

The removal of identifiers, conversion of Neurodata into features or embeddings, generation of predictions, or incorporation of Neurodata into an AI system shall not, by itself, be treated as eliminating governance obligations.

2.3. Highest applicable tier

Where more than one Neurodata Risk Tier may apply, the highest applicable tier of Functional Exposure shall govern.

2.4. Protective treatment of uncertainty

Where the information necessary to determine Functional Exposure is incomplete or uncertain, the Neurodata or Governed Artefact shall provisionally be governed under the more protective applicable tier until the uncertainty has been resolved.

2.5. Dynamic classification

Tier assignment is a continuing governance decision and not a one-time label. Classification shall be reassessed whenever the technical, institutional, jurisdictional or intended-use characteristics of the Neurodata materially change.

2.6. Proportionality

Governance safeguards shall be proportionate to the Functional Exposure of the Neurodata or Governed Artefact. Higher tiers require progressively stronger controls, specialist review and contractual protection.

2.7. Cumulative safeguards

Assignment to a higher Risk Tier does not displace safeguards associated with a lower tier where the underlying condition remains present. For example, a Tier 4 or Tier 5 artefact that remains participant-linkable shall also retain applicable linkage-key, re-identification and access safeguards associated with Tier 2; where direct identifiers or persistent participant-linked information remain, applicable Tier 3 safeguards shall also continue to apply.

The identifier and participant-linkage checks in Steps 5 and 6 shall be completed for every object within scope, including an object assigned a candidate, provisional or confirmed Tier 4 or Tier 5. These checks identify additional safeguards and shall not reduce a higher tier. Where linkage is maintained by an upstream institution or repository, record the responsible custodian and applicable access restrictions; this requirement does not authorise obtaining or disclosing the linkage key. Application to public release: The measures above are the default minimum measures for controlled-or limited-access Tier 2 arrangements, particularly where a linkage key or other reasonably available linkage mechanism exists. Where public or open release is proposed, Tool 2 (Supplementary Table 7) Step 8B may recognise documented, release-specific safeguards in place of a measure that cannot operate in an open-release pathway, but only where the assessment explains how those safeguards adequately address the same relevant risks in the proposed release context. The assessment must consider residual disclosure and linkage risk, reasonably foreseeable downstream use, release conditions and the practical enforceability of any repository or licence terms. A re-identification prohibition alone is insufficient. This pathway-specific assessment does not change the Tier 2 classification, establish that the data are legally anonymous, or remove any applicable legal, consent, ethics, institutional or upstream restriction. If the necessary protection cannot be demonstrated, use Final Decision Outcome 3 or Final Decision Outcome 4 under Tool 2 (Supplementary Table 7).

3. TIERED NEURODATA RISK CLASSIFICATION FRAMEWORK

>TIERED NEURODATA RISK CLASSIFICATION FRAMEWORK >Tier 1 -Aggregated or Functionally Non-Revealing Neurodata

3.3. Tier 3 -Directly Identifiable or Intrinsically Traceable Neurodata

Tier 3 applies where Neurodata contains direct identifiers, recognisable identifying anatomy, identifying acquisition metadata, or intrinsic signal characteristics that reasonably permit participant identification or tracing without reliance solely on a separately protected code-to-identity mapping. A raw acquisition format does not, by itself, establish Tier 3. Participant linkage maintained solely through a code, repository record or separately protected institutional mapping is assessed under Tier 2, unless a higher-tier condition also applies.

Examples (a) non-defaced structural imaging retaining recognisable facial anatomy; (b) raw DICOM files containing headers or recognisable anatomy; (c) EEG, MEG or ECoG recordings retaining identifying metadata or reasonably demonstrated intrinsic participant-tracing capacity; (d) implant telemetry or BCI recordings retaining identifying device information or intrinsic participant-tracing capacity (e) device identifiers, implant logs or precise timestamps that reasonably enable participant identification or tracing; and (f) Neurodata associated with names, voice, video or other direct identifiers. Primary concern Direct participant traceability and the exposure of sensitive neurological or health-related information. Minimum governance measures (a) storage within a secure and controlled environment; (b) encryption in storage and transit; (c) role-based access controls; (d) formal access authorisation; (e) audit logs and monitoring; (f) removal of unnecessary identifiers where feasible; (g) restrictions on downloading, copying and onward sharing; and (h) enhanced contractual and institutional oversight. 3.3.4. Tier 4 -Functionally Revealing Derivative Neurodata Description Tier 4 applies to transformed or derived Neurodata that may no longer resemble the source dataset but can reasonably reveal, predict, reconstruct or profile neurological, cognitive, emotional or behavioural states. Examples (a) neural feature vectors or embeddings; (b) neural fingerprints; (c) cognitive or behavioural profiles; (d) classifiers or predictive outputs derived from Neurodata; (e) reconstructed visual, auditory or cognitive representations; (f) synthetic Neurodata retaining meaningful neural characteristics; and (g) latent representations capable of supporting neural inference or participant reconstruction.

Primary concern

Inferential, predictive, reconstructive or profiling-related Functional Exposure. (f) models capable of participant-level inference, reconstruction or memorisation; and (g) AI systems that retain Neurodata-derived information after completion of the original research activity.

Minimum governance measures

Their technical form or incorporation of Neurodata does not automatically establish Tier 5 status.

Primary concern

Persistent and potentially difficult-to-reverse computational exposure, including memorisation, inversion, retraining, repurposing and loss of meaningful downstream control.

Minimum governance measures

4.1.2.

The assessment shall concern the specific Neurodata object or Governed Artefact that will be stored, accessed, analysed, shared, transferred, transformed, reused or deployed, rather than the original research project or source dataset as a whole. Object-specific classification does not determine or extinguish conditions arising from the source data's provenance, Applicable Law, consent, ethics approvals or upstream agreements. The applicability of those conditions to the object and proposed activity shall be assessed separately and recorded in Schedules B-D, as appropriate.

4.1.3

4.1.4.

The final Risk Tier shall be the highest tier identified during the assessment.

4.1.5. Tier terminology.

A candidate tier identifies evidence that may support a particular Risk Tier and requires further assessment; it is not itself a final tier assignment. A provisional tier is a temporary protective classification applied while material uncertainty remains. A confirmed tier is assigned once the relevant assessment has established that the applicable Functional Exposure criteria are met.

4.1.6. Interpretation of "reasonably".

A capacity is reasonably foreseeable where it is supported by relevant empirical evidence, established methods, or a credible technical assessment of methods feasible in the proposed access and use environment. Assessment shall consider the object's characteristics, available methods, expertise, resources, access rights and additional information reasonably available to the intended recipient. Published findings shall be assessed for their applicability to the particular object and environment. Demonstration in the current project is not required, but a purely speculative possibility is insufficient. Where a material capacity cannot be assessed reliably, the answer shall be "Unknown", with the applicable provisional safeguards and review requirements.

7.2. Derivative and Embedding Governance Decision Tool

The Derivative and Embedding Governacne Decision Tool shall be completed where: The Tool determines whether the transformation has altered Functional Exposure or requires a revised Risk Tier or additional safeguards.

Routine-processing and Tier 1 exception. Completion of the Derivative and Embedding Governance Decision Tool is not required solely because routine preprocessing has occurred without creating a separately governed derivative or materially altering Functional Exposure. The Tool is also not required for the assessment of a confirmed Tier 1 aggregate or summary-level output where the documented assessment establishes that the output contains no participant-level record, persistent participant trace, linkage mechanism, material inferential exposure or model-associated computational persistence.

The use of features, embeddings of predictive models to calculate such an output does not, by itself, remove this exception. Source data, retained intermediate representations and models shall be assessed separately where they constitute distinct governance objects. The exception does not apply to those objects, to proposed AI or model activities covered by Annexure 2 Step 10, or where uncertainty remains concerning the output's Functional Exposure. A subsequent transformation, linkage, recipient change or proposed use capable of materially altering Functional Exposure requires reassessment and, where applicable, completion of Annexure 3.

Following completion of the applicable governance assessments, the MDTAA Clause Selection Tool shall be used to translate the identified:

8. ORDER OF APPLICATION

Unless the circumstances require reassessment of an earlier decision, the governance tools shall ordinarily be applied in the following sequence: 1.

Neurodata Governance Decision Tool -classify the Neurodata object and assign the applicable Risk Tier. 2. Transfer and Access Decision Tool -assess any proposed external sharing, repository access, remote access or cross-border pathway. 3. Derivative and Embedding Governance Decision Tool -assess technical transformation, derivative artefacts and AI or model embedding. 4. MDTAA Clause Selection Tool -implement the resulting governance decisions through the appropriate MDTAA contractual modules.

Completion of a later tool may require the Parties to return to and repeat an earlier assessment where new information indicates that the Functional Exposure or proposed governance pathway has changed.
