This outcome applies only where the applicable lawful basis and transfer or access mechanism have been confirmed, all mandatory assessments have been completed, and all approvals and authority required for the proposed transfer, access or release have been obtained and documented, but specified supplementary safeguards remain to be implemented within the current pathway.

Pending approvals, incomplete mandatory assessments and unconfirmed lawful bases, transfer or access mechanisms, or authority for the proposed activity do not qualify for this outcome.

The proposed transfer, access or release shall not commence until the supplementary safeguards have been implemented, documented and verified. Following verification, the Parties shall return to Step 13 and record Outcome 1 only if all its conditions are satisfied.

3.3. Outcome 3 -Redesign the transfer or access pathway

The proposed pathway shall be redesigned where its risks cannot be adequately managed in its current form but may be reduced through a more protective access model, narrower recipient group, stronger contractual control or different technical environment.

3.4. Outcome 4 -Do not proceed

The proposed pathway shall not proceed where:

4.4.

Where a single arrangement involves several recipients or subprocessors, the assessment may be completed collectively only where all recipients are subject to substantially equivalent governance conditions.

4.4A.

Multiple objects. Where a single arrangement involves more than one Neurodata object or Governed Artefact and those objects share the same recipients, jurisdictions, access model, downstream purpose and governance environment, a single Neuro-TADT may cover them collectively provided each object is separately identified. Unless the objects are demonstrably segregated, the safeguards applicable to the highest-risk object shall govern the shared pathway.

4.5.

Any answer marked "Unsure" or "Unknown" shall be resolved before the transfer or access arrangement proceeds. The assessment may continue in order to identify additional risks and safeguards, but no final pathway outcome shall be recorded while a material uncertainty remains unless the relevant step expressly requires Outcome 4.

4.6.

The outcome and supporting reasons shall be recorded in the relevant MDTAA Schedule.

9. RELATIONSHIP WITH THE OTHER MDTAA GOVERNANCE TOOLS

>RELATIONSHIP WITH THE OTHER MDTAA GOVERNANCE TOOLS

9.1. Annexure 1 -Neurodata Governance Decision Tool

Annexure 1 determines the nature and Functional Exposure of the Neurodata or Governed Artefact and assigns the applicable Risk Tier.

The Neuro-TADT then assesses whether the proposed transfer or access pathway can preserve the protection required for that tier. 1.2. The purpose of this Annexure is to determine whether a technical transformation has altered the governance status, Functional Exposure or applicable Neurodata Risk Tier of Neurodata or a Governed Artefact. 1.3. This Annexure applies whenever Neurodata are subjected to technical transformation, including: (a) feature extraction; (b) embedding generation; (c) dimensionality reduction; (d) latent representation generation; (e) predictive modelling; (f) classification or profiling; (g) reconstruction; (h) synthetic Neurodata generation; (i) AI or machine-learning training, fine-tuning, validation or benchmarking; (j) federated learning; (k) model-weight generation or updating; or (l) incorporation into another persistent computational system. 2.2. Independent governance object A derivative, embedding, model, synthetic dataset or other transformed output shall be treated as an independent governance object where it: (a) can circulate independently of the source Neurodata; (b) can be accessed, shared, licensed, transferred or deployed separately; (c) has an independent retention period or downstream purpose; (d) supports inference, prediction, reconstruction or profiling; or (e) persists within an AI model or computational infrastructure.

9.2. Annexure 3 -Neural Derivative and Embedding Governance Decision Tool

>Annexure 3 -Neural Derivative and Embedding Governance Decision Tool

2.3. Functional Exposure governs classification

The governance status of a transformed object shall be determined by what the object can reveal or enable, rather than solely by its file format, mathematical representation, legal description or degree of technical abstraction.

2.4. Highest applicable tier

Where a transformed output exhibits characteristics associated with more than one Risk Tier, the highest applicable tier shall govern.

2.5. Protective treatment of uncertainty

Where the inferential, reconstructive, memorisation, inversion or linkage capacity of a transformed output is uncertain, the output shall provisionally be governed under the more protective applicable tier until specialist review has been completed.

2.6. Continuing provenance

The provenance relationship between the transformed output and the source Neurodata shall be documented and maintained throughout the lifecycle of the output.

2.7. No governance circumvention

Technical transformation shall not be used to avoid, reduce or circumvent governance obligations that remain proportionate to the Functional Exposure of the transformed output.

3. POSSIBLE OUTCOMES

The Tool shall produce one of the following outcomes.

3.1. Retain the existing Risk Tier

The original Risk Tier may be retained where the transformed output: (a) does not materially increase Functional Exposure; (b) cannot reasonably support participant-level inference, reconstruction, profiling or linkage beyond the source object; (c) does not preserve material neural information within a persistent model or computational system; and (d) remains subject to governance safeguards proportionate to its actual capabilities.

The decision and technical justification shall be documented.

3.2. Refer for Tier 4 reassessment

The transformed output shall be classified or provisionally classified as Tier 4 -Functionally Revealing Derivative Neurodata where it can reasonably support:

3.3. Confirm or provisionally classify as Tier 5

The transformed output shall be classified or provisionally classified as Tier 5 -Model-Embedded or Computationally Persistent Neurodata where neural information has become materially embedded within:

3.4. Specialist review required

Specialist review shall be required where: (g) the output may be used for high-impact or materially different purposes; or (h) the appropriate Risk Tier remains contested or unclear.

3.5. Do not proceed where the identified exposure cannot be governed

Incorporation into an AI model or persistent computational infrastructure does not automatically determine Tier 5 status. Tier 5 reassessment requires evidence, or reasonable uncertainty, that continuing Functional Exposure may persist. Where model incorporation is known but continuing exposure is uncertain, the classification shall remain provisional pending specialist review.

4. INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLETION

>INSTRUCTIONS FOR COMPLETION >Begin at Step 1 and follow the pathway indicated by the answer selected.

4.2.

The assessment shall concern the specific transformed output, model, embedding, prediction, synthetic dataset or computational artefact under review.

4.3.

A separate assessment should ordinarily be completed for each materially different output, model version, training run, embedding repository, synthetic dataset or deployment environment.

4.4.

The assessment shall consider both: (a) the current demonstrated capabilities of the transformed output; and (b) capabilities that are reasonably foreseeable in light of the method, architecture, training data and intended downstream use.

4.5.

Where the answer to any question is unknown, the more protective pathway shall apply until the uncertainty is resolved.

4.6.

The final Risk Tier shall be the highest tier identified through the assessment.

11. RELATIONSHIP WITH THE OTHER MDTAA GOVERNANCE TOOLS

>RELATIONSHIP WITH THE OTHER MDTAA GOVERNANCE TOOLS

11.1. Annexure 1-Neurodata Governance Decision Tool

Annexure 1 assigns the Risk Tier applicable to the source Neurodata or existing Governed Artefact. This Annexure determines whether technical transformation requires that tier to be retained, increased or reconsidered.

11.2. Annexure 2 -Neurodata Transfer and Access Decision Tool (Neuro-TADT)

Annexure 2 assesses whether an external access, transfer, repository, vendor, cloud or cross-border pathway can preserve the protection required for the transformed output.

Where a derivative or model is transferred, shared, hosted or remotely accessed, Annexure 2 shall be completed or updated using the revised Risk Tier produced under this Annexure.

11.3. MDTAA Clause Selection Tool

The MDTAA Clause Selection Tool shall translate the outcome of this Annexure into appropriate contractual provisions concerning: >GOVERNING PRINCIPLES

2.1. Governance decisions must be contractually implemented

A governance measure identified through Annexures 1-3 shall not be treated as operationally complete unless it is reflected, where appropriate, in:

2.2. Modular and proportionate drafting

The MDTAA shall be assembled proportionately by activating only those modules required for the specific Neurodata, recipient, access model, jurisdiction, infrastructure, transformation and downstream purpose.

2.3. Higher-risk Neurodata requires stronger contractual protection

Neurodata assigned to Tier 3, Tier 4 or Tier 5 shall require enhanced contractual safeguards reflecting the greater Functional Exposure associated with direct traceability, derivative inference or computational persistence.

2.4. Technical safeguards must be supported by contractual controls

Where the preceding decision tools require technical controls, including controlled access, audit logging, prohibition of reconstruction, AI-use restrictions or deletion measures, the MDTAA shall allocate responsibility for implementing, maintaining, verifying and enforcing those controls.

2.5. No unresolved governance gaps

The MDTAA shall not be signed where a material governance issue identified through Annexures 1-3 remains unresolved, including uncertainty regarding:

5.20. Contractual Coordination and Precedence Module

For upstream instruments, record their applicability to source data, derivatives, aggregates and models, and any approval, redistribution or surviving-use conditions. The Parties cannot amend or waive an external instrument through the MDTAA without the authority and approvals required by that instrument. Where an inconsistency remains unresolved, suspend the affected activity and obtain clarification, amendment or approval from the authorised body.

9. RELATIONSHIP WITH THE GOVERNANCE TOOLKIT

The governance toolkit shall ordinarily be applied in the following sequence: 1.

Annexure 1: determine what the Neurodata or Governed Artefact is and assign the applicable Risk Tier; 2. Annexure 2: determine whether the proposed transfer or access pathway can preserve the protection required for that tier; 3. Annexure 3: determine whether technical transformation, derivatives, embeddings or AI systems alter the governance status or Risk Tier; and 4. Annexure 4: translate those governance decisions into enforceable MDTAA modules. The MDTAA Clause Selection Tool therefore completes the governance workflow by converting classification, transfer and transformation decisions into binding contractual obligations.

Supplementary Data Legends

Supplementary Data 1 | Legal corpus inventory. Inventory of 477 legal-instrument and governance-document entries reviewed across 93 sovereign jurisdictions and 10 North American operative governance units. Entries are not necessarily unique enactments; shared instruments may appear in multiple governance profiles.

Supplementary Data 2 | Directional transfer-compatibility matrix.

A 93 × 93 matrix covering 43 African, 24 European, and 26 Latin American and Caribbean jurisdictions. Rows identify exporting jurisdictions and columns identify receiving jurisdictions. Entries assign compatibility classes A1-E; self-transfers are excluded. North American operative governance units are not included. The matrix underpins main Figure 3.

Supplementary Data 3 | Jurisdiction-level comparative coding.

Coded governance variables for the 93 sovereign jurisdictions, supporting the regional descriptive distributions in main Figure 2 and the qualitative synthesis in Supplementary Tables 2 and 3. North American operative governance units are analysed separately.

Supplementary Figure 2 provides an unweighted schematic of regional governance contexts, including North America. Arrows identify directions requiring separate assessment and do not rank transfer compatibility. Supplementary Table 4 identifies contextual considerations for each direction, and Supplementary Table 5 sets out the assessment domains. Directional compatibility findings for the 93 sovereign jurisdictions are reported in main Figure 3 and Supplementary Data 2.

Together, these materials support the conclusion that international neurodata sharing is characterised by conditional interoperability rather than by a simple distinction between permissible and prohibited transfer. Where a pathway is legally available, its practical navigability may still depend on the coordinated operation of legal, institutional, repository and contractual safeguards within the relevant originating and receiving environments. This regional synthesis concerns the transfer, safeguard, enforcement and contractual domains examined through the comparative coding. It does not establish whether legal protection persists, weakens or changes after neurodata are transformed into derivatives, embeddings or model-associated artefacts; those post-transformation questions are addressed later through the paper's normative and methodological extension.

Supplementary Figure 2 | Regional governance contexts for directional neurodata transfer assessment. Nodes summarise the four regional analytical groupings. Arrows indicate directions in which transfer conditions must be assessed separately; their appearance does not encode relative compatibility, permissiveness or governance quality. Regional descriptions identify broad Supplementary Table 5: Assessment domains informing the regional transfer schematic. These domains organise qualitative assessment and are not assigned numerical scores or summed into a regional compatibility ranking.

PREAMBLE

Recognising the rapid development of neuroscience, neurotechnologies, and digital health systems.

Acknowledging the ethical imperatives of safeguarding mental privacy, cognitive liberty and personal dignity.

Acknowledging the FAIR and CARE principles and their role in responsible, equitable, and interoperable scientific data governance.

Desiring to promote trustworthy sharing and re-use of neurodata for scientific advancement and public benefit. Recalling the principles set forth in the Universal Declaration on Bioethics and Human Rights (UNESCO 2005), the Convention 108+ of the Council of Europe, the African Union Convention on Cybersecurity and Personal Data Protection (Malabo 2014), the OECD Privacy Guidelines 2022, and comparable regional frameworks.

Where a transfer falls within the scope of Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914, the Parties shall incorporate the applicable European Union Standard Contractual Clauses ("SCCs") as a separate, unmodified instrument, select the appropriate SCC Module and options, and complete the required SCC Annexes. The SCCs supplement the MDTAA only for transfers falling within their legal scope.

The MDTAA is published as a model agreement and governance template. The final legally binding agreement is created only once the relevant schedules have been completed and executed by authorised representatives of the participating institutions, and the undersigned parties hereby agree as follows:

5A.1. Requirement for Ethical Approval

All transfers of human-derived neurodata shall be subject to prior approval by a relevant ethics committee or institutional review board (IRB/REC), unless a documented exemption applies under local law.

5A.2. Importer's Ethical Compliance Obligations

The Data Importer shall: (a) maintain ongoing compliance with applicable human subjects and clinical research legislation; (b) report major protocol deviations, adverse events, breaches, or ethics concerns to the Data Exporter; (c) provide copies of its ethics approvals, renewal letters, or exemptions.

5A.3. Updates, Amendments, and Continuing Review

The Data Importer must notify the Data Exporter of any: (a) amendments to protocol, (b) changes in study team composition, (c) new AI/ML methods that alter the risk profile, (d) ethics committee recommendations or conditions.

5A.4. Community and context-specific requirements

Where the project involves Indigenous peoples, community-governed data, defined populations, patient groups or communities with recognised governance interests, the Parties shall identify and comply with applicable community approvals, cultural protocols, data-sovereignty requirements, benefit-sharing commitments and continuing governance conditions. These requirements shall be recorded in Schedule A or B and implemented through the Community, Collective and Indigenous Data Governance Module.

5A.5. Suspension for Ethical Non-compliance

Where ethical approval is withdrawn or materially modified, the Data Exporter may suspend transfers until full compliance is restored.

Clause 8 -Data Protection Safeguards

The data exporter warrants that it has used reasonable efforts to determine that the data importer is able, through the implementation of appropriate technical and organisational measures, to satisfy its obligations under these Clauses.

8.1. Purpose Limitation

The data importer shall process the personal data only for the specific purpose(s) of the transfer, as set out in Schedule B. It may only process the personal data for another purpose: (i) where it has obtained the data subject's prior consent; (ii) where necessary for the establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims in the context of specific administrative, regulatory or judicial proceedings; or (iii) (iii) where necessary in order to protect the vital interests of the data subject or of another natural person.

8.2. Transparency

(a) In order to enable data subjects to effectively exercise their rights pursuant to Clause 10, the data importer shall inform them, either directly or through the data exporter: (i) of its identity and contact details; (ii) of the categories of personal data processed; (iii) of the right to obtain a copy of these Clauses; (iv) where it intends to onward transfer the personal data to any third party/ies, of the recipient or categories of recipients (as appropriate with a view to providing meaningful information), the purpose of such onward transfer and the ground therefore pursuant to Clause 8.7.

(b) Paragraph (a) shall not apply where the data subject already has the information, including when such information has already been provided by the data exporter, or providing the information proves impossible or would involve a disproportionate effort for the data importer. In the latter case, the data importer shall, to the extent possible, make the information publicly available.

(c) On request, the Parties shall make a copy of these Clauses, including the Appendix as completed by them, available to the data subject free of charge. To the extent necessary to protect business secrets or other confidential information, including personal data, the Parties may redact part of the text of the Appendix prior to sharing a copy, but shall provide a meaningful summary where the data subject would otherwise not be able to understand its content or exercise his/her rights. On request, the Parties shall provide the data subject with the reasons for the redactions, to the extent possible without revealing the redacted information. The Parties shall be able to demonstrate compliance with these Clauses. In particular, the data importer shall keep appropriate documentation on the processing activities carried out on behalf of the data exporter.

(c) The data importer shall make available to the data exporter all information necessary to demonstrate compliance with the obligations set out in these Clauses and at the data exporter's request, allow for and contribute to audits of the processing activities covered by these Clauses, at reasonable intervals or if there are indications of non-compliance. In deciding on a review or audit, the data exporter may consider relevant certifications held by the data importer.

(d) The data exporter may choose to conduct the audit by itself or mandate an independent auditor. Audits may include inspections at the premises or physical facilities of the data importer and shall, where appropriate, be carried out with reasonable notice.

(e)

The Parties shall make the information referred to in paragraphs (b) and (c), including the results of any audits, available to the competent supervisory authority on request.

8.1. Instructions (a)

The data exporter has informed the data importer that it acts as processor under the instructions of its controller(s), which the data exporter shall make available to the data importer prior to processing.

(b)

The data importer shall process the personal data only on documented instructions from the controller, as communicated to the data importer by the data exporter, and any additional documented instructions from the data exporter. Such additional instructions shall not conflict with the instructions from the controller. The controller or data exporter may give further documented instructions regarding the data processing throughout the duration of the contract.

(c) The data importer shall immediately inform the data exporter if it is unable to follow those instructions.

Where the data importer is unable to follow the instructions from the controller, the data exporter shall immediately notify the controller.

(d) The data exporter warrants that it has imposed the same data protection obligations on the data importer as set out in the contract or other legal act under Union or Member State law between the controller and the data exporter 8.2.

Purpose limitation

The data importer shall process the personal data only for the specific purpose(s) of the transfer, as set out in Schedule B, unless on further instructions from the controller, as communicated to the data importer by the data exporter, or from the data exporter.

8.3. Transparency

On request, the data exporter shall make a copy of these Clauses, including the Appendix as completed by the Parties, available to the data subject free of charge. To the extent necessary to protect business secrets or other confidential information, including personal data, the data exporter may redact part of the text of the Appendix prior to sharing a copy, but shall provide a meaningful summary where the data subject would otherwise not be able to understand its content or exercise his/her rights. On request, the Parties shall provide the data subject with the reasons for the redactions, to the extent possible without revealing the redacted information.

ARTICLE 13 -GOVERNMENT ACCESS REQUESTS & OVERSIGHT

13.1. General Principle The Parties acknowledge that Data Importers in certain jurisdictions may receive requests from public authorities for access to Personal Data or Neurodata transferred under this Agreement. The obligations contained in Clause 15 of the EU Standard Contractual Clauses therefore apply fully and are incorporated verbatim below. These obligations must be read together with Article 12 of this Agreement (Local Laws and Transfer Impact Assessments) and Clauses 14 and 16 of the SCCs. 13.2. EU SCC Clause 15 (Verbatim Text) Clause 15 -Obligations of the data importer in case of access by public authorities MODULE ONE: Transfer controller to controller MODULE TWO: Transfer controller to processor MODULE THREE: Transfer processor to processor MODULE FOUR: Transfer processor to controller (where the EU processor combines the personal data received from the third country-controller with personal data collected by the processor in the EU) 15.1. Notification (a)

The data importer agrees to notify the data exporter and, where possible, the data subject promptly (if necessary with the help of the data exporter) if it: (i) receives a legally binding request from a public authority, including judicial authorities, under the laws of the country of destination for the disclosure of personal data transferred pursuant to these Clauses; such notification shall include information about the personal data requested, the requesting authority, the legal basis for the request and the response provided; or (ii) becomes aware of any direct access by public authorities to personal data transferred pursuant to these Clauses in accordance with the laws of the country of destination; such notification shall include all information available to the importer.

[For Module Three: The data exporter shall forward the notification to the controller.] (b) If the data importer is prohibited from notifying the data exporter and/or the data subject under the laws of the country of destination, the data importer agrees to use its best efforts to obtain a waiver of the prohibition, with a view to communicating as much information as possible, as soon as possible. The data importer agrees to document its best efforts in order to be able to demonstrate them on request of the data exporter.

(c) Where permissible under the laws of the country of destination, the data importer agrees to provide the data exporter, at regular intervals for the duration of the contract, with as much relevant information as possible on the requests received (in particular, number of requests, type of data requested, requesting authority/ies, whether requests have been challenged and the outcome of such challenges, etc.).

[For Module Three: The data exporter shall forward the information to the controller.] 13A.

ARTICLE 13A -NEURODATA TRANSFER AND ACCESS DECISION TOOL (NEURO-TADT)

1. Purpose The Neuro-TADT assesses whether a proposed transfer or access pathway has the capacity to implement and maintain the safeguards required for the Risk Tier assigned under Article 10A and Annexure 1.13A.2. Application The Neuro-TADT shall be completed before Neurodata or a Governed Artefact is: (a) shared with another institution or external collaborator; (b) transferred across a national or jurisdictional border; (c) accessed remotely from another legal jurisdiction; (d) deposited in or accessed through a repository; (e) hosted or processed by a cloud provider, vendor or commercial partner; (f) processed through federated, query-only, model-to-data or distributed infrastructure; or (g) otherwise made accessible outside the originating Party's internal governance environment. 13A.3. Preconditions Before assessing safeguard capacity, the Parties shall confirm and record: (a) the lawful basis for the proposed processing; (b) the transfer or access mechanism relied upon; (c) the relevant consent conditions; (d) required legal, ethics, institutional, repository, DAC or regulatory approvals; and (e) the applicable Risk Tier under Article 10A and Annexure 1. Completion of the Neuro-TADT does not itself establish that the activity is lawful. 13A.4. Assessment The Neuro-TADT shall examine: (a) all recipients and subprocessors; (b) the originating, receiving, hosting and remotely accessing jurisdictions; (c) the access model and whether a downloadable copy will be created; (d) the repository, cloud or computational infrastructure; (e) the receiving environment's capacity to implement, verify and maintain the Required Safeguards; (f) proposed dataset linkage; (g) derivative generation or AI use; (h) materially different downstream purposes; (i) onward sharing; (j) oversight, audit, incident-response and remedial arrangements; and (k) any uncertainty capable of affecting Continuity of Protection.

This assessment does not constitute a finding of formal legal equivalence or adequacy.

13A.5. Dataset linkage

Where dataset linkage is planned, Annexure 1 shall be reapplied before the linkage occurs. The Neuro-TADT shall then be reconsidered using the resulting provisional classification and Required Safeguards.

13A.6. Transformation and AI use The data importer shall be liable to the data subject, and the data subject shall be entitled to receive compensation, for any material or non-material damages the data importer or its sub-processor causes the data subject by breaching the third-party beneficiary rights under these Clauses.

(c) Notwithstanding paragraph (b), the data exporter shall be liable to the data subject, and the data subject shall be entitled to receive compensation, for any material or non-material damages the data exporter or the data importer (or its sub-processor) causes the data subject by breaching the third-party beneficiary rights under these Clauses. This is without prejudice to the liability of the data exporter and, where the data exporter is a processor acting on behalf of a controller, to the liability of the controller under Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or Regulation (EU) 2018/1725, as applicable.

(d) The Parties agree that if the data exporter is held liable under paragraph (c) for damages caused by the data importer (or its sub-processor), it shall be entitled to claim back from the data importer that part of the compensation corresponding to the data importer's responsibility for the damage.

(e) Where more than one Party is responsible for any damage caused to the data subject as a result of a breach of these Clauses, all responsible Parties shall be jointly and severally liable and the data subject is entitled to bring an action in court against any of these Parties.

(f) The Parties agree that if one Party is held liable under paragraph (e), it shall be entitled to claim back from the other Party/ies that part of the compensation corresponding to its/their responsibility for the damage.

(g) The data importer may not invoke the conduct of a sub-processor to avoid its own liability.

14.3. Relationship With Other MDTA Provisions 14.3.1. In the event of any conflict between this Article and any other provision of this Agreement, the liability framework of the SCCs shall prevail to the extent required to guarantee an equivalent level of protection under Regulation (EU) 2016/679.14.3.2. Nothing in this Article shall be interpreted as limiting Data Subjects' rights under Article 11 of this Agreement or SCC Clause 10 (Data Subject Rights). 14.3.3. This Article shall not limit any additional remedies agreed by the Parties under Article 15 (Indemnity) or Article 16 (Dispute Resolution), except where such limitation would diminish protections afforded under the SCCs. 14.3.4. The neurodata-specific protections in Articles 6-12 of this Agreement supplement, and do not replace, the liability provisions of the SCCs. 14.4. Prohibition on Liability Avoidance 14.4.1. No Party may rely on the actions or omissions of processors, sub-processors, contractors, research collaborators, or automated systems to reduce or eliminate liability under this Article. 14.4.2. Model, API and Query Access Conditions Authorised users or user categories: Authentication requirements: Permitted API or query access: Query-frequency or rate limitations: Description Tier 1 applies to aggregated, statistical or summary-level information that contains no participant-level record, persistent participant trace or linkage mechanism and presents no reasonable small-group disclosure risk. Examples (a) group-average brain-activation patterns; (b) aggregated connectivity measures; (c) summary statistics; (d) published statistical results that contain no participant-level records; and (e) sufficiently aggregated research outputs from which no individual or small group can reasonably be identified. Primary concern Verification that aggregation or anonymisation is sufficiently robust and that no participant-level trace remains. Minimum governance measures (a) document the aggregation or anonymisation method; (b) confirm that no participant-level records or linkage keys remain; (c) assess rare-condition, small-cohort and metadata-related disclosure risks; and (d) apply ordinary institutional sharing procedures unless additional risk factors are present. 3.2. Tier 2 -Pseudonymised or Participant-Level Neurodata Without Direct Identifiers Description Tier 2 applies to participant-level Neurodata from which direct identifiers have been removed, whether or not a linkage mechanism is reasonably available to the relevant actor in the assessed context. The assessment shall record whether linkage is reasonably available to the originating institution, the intended recipient and, where public release is proposed, foreseeable downstream users. Tier 2 remains a governance classification and does not determine whether the information is legally personal, anonymous, or otherwise regulated. Where direct identifiers, intrinsic traceability, or another Tier 3 or higher condition applies, assign the applicable higher tier. Examples (a) pseudonymised EEG or MEG data linked to a participant code; (b) de-identified MRI data capable of re-linkage through a secure institutional key; (c) participant-level processed Neurodata held in a controlled repository; and (d) coded behavioural-neural datasets. Primary concern Residual identification, traceability, disclosure, and inference risk in the assessed context, including the availability of linkage mechanisms and auxiliary information. Minimum governance measures (a) controlled access; (b) separation and protection of linkage keys; 5.2. Where a provisional tier has been assigned, the uncertainty and the measures required to resolve it shall also be recorded. 5.3. No external access, transfer, repository deposit, AI deployment or materially different reuse shall occur until the minimum safeguards associated with the assigned tier have been implemented. 6. REASSESSMENT 6.1. The assigned Risk Tier shall be reassessed whenever the Neurodata or Governed Artefact: (a) is linked with an additional dataset; (b) is transformed into a feature, embedding, profile, classifier, prediction, synthetic dataset, model or other derivative representation; (c) is incorporated into or extracted from an AI or machine-learning system; (d) is reused for a new or materially different research purpose; (e) is transferred to or accessed by a new institution, repository, vendor or jurisdiction; (f) is moved into a new cloud, repository, secure-computing or distributed computational environment; (g) becomes accessible to a new recipient or subprocessor; (h) acquires new inferential, predictive, reconstructive or profiling capabilities; (i) becomes subject to materially different legal, ethical, contractual or repository conditions; or (j) is otherwise affected by a change capable of altering its Functional Exposure. 6.2. Reassessment is not limited to determining whether the Neurodata have become more identifiable. It shall consider whether the object's capacity to support tracing, inference, reconstruction, profiling, prediction, memorisation, inversion or downstream harm has changed. 6.3. Where reassessment results in a higher Risk Tier: (a) the higher tier shall apply immediately; (b) any continued processing, access or transfer shall be suspended where the necessary safeguards are not yet in place; (c) Schedule B shall be updated; and (d) the relevant MDTAA modules shall be reconsidered using the MDTAA Clause Selection Tool. 6.4. A lower tier may be assigned only where the Party responsible for governance can document that the relevant Functional Exposure has materially and reliably decreased.

1.6.

Completion of the Neuro-TADT does not establish that a proposed transfer or access arrangement is lawful. The Parties remain responsible for confirming compliance with Applicable Law, ethics approvals, consent conditions, institutional requirements, repository rules, regulatory authorisations and all applicable contractual obligations.

2.1. Continuity of Protection

A proposed transfer or access pathway shall be permitted only where the safeguards applicable to the assigned Neurodata Risk Tier can be preserved throughout the receiving legal, institutional, repository, technical and computational environment.

2.2. Legal authorisation is not sufficient

The existence of a lawful transfer mechanism, contractual agreement, participant consent, ethics approval or repository authorisation does not, by itself, establish that the proposed pathway preserves Continuity of Protection.

2.3. Pathway-specific assessment

The Neuro-TADT shall assess the actual proposed arrangement, including: (i) the safeguards implemented by the receiving environment.

2.4. Capacity to maintain Required Safeguards

The assessment shall determine whether the receiving legal, institutional, repository, technical and computational environment has the capacity to implement, verify and maintain the safeguards required for the assigned Risk Tier. This assessment does not constitute a finding of formal legal equivalence or adequacy.

2.5. Protective treatment of uncertainty

Where the identity of a recipient, subprocessor, destination environment, downstream purpose or technical use is unknown, the transfer or access arrangement shall not proceed until the uncertainty has been resolved.

2.6. Preference for controlled access

Where the capacity to implement and maintain the safeguards required for the assigned tier cannot be demonstrated for a downloadable transfer, the Parties shall consider whether the pathway can be redesigned through:

2.7. Highest applicable safeguard

Where the proposed pathway involves multiple recipients, jurisdictions, platforms or processing activities, the safeguards applicable to the highest-risk component shall govern the arrangement as a whole unless the relevant components are demonstrably segregated.

3. NEURO-TADT OUTCOMES

The Neuro-TADT shall result in one of the following four outcomes.

3.1. Outcome 1 -Proceed

The proposed transfer or access pathway may proceed where: (a) all relevant recipients and subprocessors have been identified; (b) the pathway is legally and institutionally authorised; (c) the receiving environment provides functionally equivalent protection; (d) no unresolved downstream risks have been identified; and (e) all safeguards required for the assigned Neurodata Risk Tier are in place.

3.2. Outcome 2 -Proceed after supplementary safeguards are implemented 5. NEURODATA TRANSFER AND ACCESS DECISION WORKFLOW Supplementary Table 7 | Neurodata Transfer and Access Decision Tool (Neuro-TADT).

Supplementary safeguards may include: (a) replacing downloadable access with secure remote access; (b) stronger encryption or key-management measures; (c) stricter role-based access controls; (d) enhanced access and output logging; (e) prohibition or restriction of dataset linkage; (f) prohibition or restriction of AI training, fine-tuning or profiling; (g) prior approval for onward sharing; (h) contractual flow-down obligations; (i) repository or secure-environment controls; (j) additional ethics, legal or institutional oversight; (k) enhanced incident reporting and audit rights; (l) shortened retention periods; (m) deletion certification; or (n) other tier-appropriate safeguards. For each outstanding supplementary safeguard, the Parties shall record the required action, responsible party, implementation deadline and evidence required for verification. The proposed transfer, access or release shall not commence until all such safeguards have been implemented, documented and verified. Where a required prerequisite remains pending or unconfirmed, the assessment shall remain pending while the necessary decision or evidence is obtained. If a final outcome must be recorded before resolution, Outcome 4 shall apply. A pending prerequisite does not, by itself, establish that the proposed activity is unlawful.

A requirement to obtain separate approval for a future onward transfer may be recorded as a continuing safeguard only where that onward transfer is excluded from the presently authorised activity and is prohibited until the separate approval has been obtained.

6.3. Redesign the transfer or access pathway

This outcome applies where the proposed arrangement does not presently preserve Continuity of Protection but may become acceptable through material modification.

Redesign may include: (a) changing from data transfer to controlled remote access; (b) using a trusted research environment; (c) limiting the categories or volume of Neurodata disclosed; (d) providing aggregated or less revealing outputs; (e) removing unnecessary identifiers or metadata; (f) separating linkage keys; (g) limiting recipients; (h) replacing an unsuitable vendor or platform; (i) prohibiting downstream AI use; (j) changing the destination jurisdiction or institution; or (k) restructuring the research workflow through federated or query-only analysis.

Following redesign, the Neuro-TADT shall be repeated.

6.4. Do not proceed

The decision shall be Do not proceed where identified risks cannot be reduced to an acceptable level or where the Parties cannot demonstrate that the proposed pathway is lawful, governable, auditable and capable of preserving protection appropriate to the assigned tier.

If the artefact, model, access arrangement or purpose is redesigned, repeat the affected assessments before proceeding. 6. FINAL DECISION 6.1. Retain existing Risk Tier The existing Risk Tier may be retained where: (a) the transformation has not materially increased Functional Exposure; (b) the output does not support material participant-level inference, reconstruction or profiling; (c) no material neural information has been embedded in a persistent computational system; (d) independent circulation does not introduce additional governance risk; and (e) the technical justification has been documented.

Retention of the existing tier shall not remove the requirement to apply the safeguards already associated with that tier.

6.2. Reclassify as Tier 4

The output shall be reclassified as Tier 4 where it: (a) supports neurological, cognitive, emotional or behavioural inference; (b) enables reconstruction, profiling, prediction or singling out; (c) retains a meaningful representation of participant-level neural characteristics; or (d) creates a functionally revealing derivative capable of independent circulation or downstream use.

6.3. Confirm Tier 5 classification

The output shall be classified as Tier 5 where the completed assessment demonstrates that neural information is materially embedded within a model or persistent computational system and that the resulting artefact retains continuing Functional Exposure through inference, reconstruction, extraction, profiling, memorisation, prediction or another consequential use. Independent reuse, querying, copying, fine-tuning or deployment may provide evidence relevant to that assessment but does not, by itself, confirm Tier 5. Where continuing persistence or Functional Exposure cannot be determined with sufficient confidence, the artefact shall remain provisionally governed under Tier 5 safeguards and proceed to specialist review under section 6.4.

6.4. Specialist review required

Specialist review shall be required where the final classification cannot be determined with sufficient confidence.

The review may include: (a) technical testing; (b) model inversion or membership-inference testing; (c) disclosure-risk analysis; (d) AI-governance review; (e) legal or ethics review; (f) cybersecurity review; (g) vendor or infrastructure due diligence; or (h) another relevant expert assessment. 6.5. Do not proceed The transformation, use, sharing or deployment shall not proceed where: 263 3. (a) the Functional Exposure cannot be adequately understood; (b) material inferential or model-persistence risks cannot be governed; (c) provenance cannot be established; (d) recipients or infrastructure providers cannot be identified; (e) required restrictions cannot be enforced; (f) the intended purpose is unauthorised; or (g) the Parties cannot implement safeguards proportionate to the resulting tier. 7. MINIMUM GOVERNANCE REQUIREMENTS FOR TIER 4 DERIVATIVES Where the transformed output is classified as Tier 4, the following minimum measures shall apply unless stronger measures are required: (a) controlled access; (b) documented source-data and transformation provenance; (c) documented purpose and approved downstream uses; (d) restrictions on unauthorised inference, profiling, prediction and reconstruction; (e) restrictions on linkage with additional datasets; (f) restrictions on general-purpose AI training; (g) restrictions on onward sharing and independent circulation; (h) access and use logging; (i) output review or disclosure controls where appropriate; (j) recipient and user authentication; (k) retention and deletion requirements; (l) incident reporting; (m) audit and compliance rights; and (n) reassessment before materially different reuse.

8. MINIMUM GOVERNANCE REQUIREMENTS FOR TIER 5 ARTEFACTS

Where the transformed output is classified as Tier 5, the following minimum measures shall apply unless stronger measures are required: (a) all

Tier 4 safeguards; (b) specialist AI and model-governance review; (c) documentation of the model architecture, version and purpose; 264 3. (d) documentation of training-data provenance; (e) identification of cloud providers, vendors and subprocessors; (f) restrictions on copying, export, redistribution and deployment; (g) restrictions on retraining, fine-tuning and transfer learning; (h) restrictions on model merging, distillation and derivative-model creation; (i) testing or assessment for memorisation, extraction, inversion and membership inference; (j) controls governing prompts, queries, outputs and API access where relevant; (k) technical and contractual restrictions on unauthorised downstream use; (l) defined model-retention and decommissioning procedures; (m) deletion, withdrawal or model-unlearning procedures where technically feasible; (n) monitoring for material capability changes; (o) version control and change management; (p) continuing auditability; and (q) approval before external transfer, deployment or access. 9. REQUIRED RECORD OF ASSESSMENT 9.1. The Party responsible for completing this Annexure shall record: (a) the source Neurodata; (b) the original Risk Tier assigned under Annexure 1; (c) the transformation performed; (d) the technical method, software or model used; (e) the transformed output or Governed Artefact produced; (f) whether the output can circulate independently; (g) whether participant linkage remains possible; (h) whether the output supports inference, reconstruction, profiling or prediction; (i) whether neural information is embedded in a model or persistent infrastructure; (j) the resulting Risk Tier; (k) any unresolved uncertainty; (l) the safeguards required; (m) whether Annexure 2 must be completed or updated; (n) the final decision; (o) the justification for that decision; 265 3. (p) the date of assessment; and (q) the person or governance body responsible for approval. 9.2. The record shall also identify: (a) all versions of the transformed output to which the assessment applies; (b) any restrictions on reuse, sharing, deployment or model updating; and (c) the circumstances that will trigger reassessment. 10. REASSESSMENT AND CHANGE CONTROL 10.1. This Annexure shall be repeated or updated where: (a) the transformation method changes; (b) the source Neurodata or training dataset changes; (c) the model architecture or version changes materially; (d) the artefact is fine-tuned, retrained or merged with another model; (e) new datasets are linked or added; (f) new inferential or reconstructive capabilities are discovered; (g) the artefact is transferred, shared or deployed in a new environment; (h) a new vendor, provider or subprocessor is introduced; (i) the intended purpose changes; (j) the artefact becomes independently accessible; (k) deletion, withdrawal or unlearning becomes more or less feasible; (l) a security incident or unauthorised use occurs; or (m) new evidence indicates that the existing Risk Tier no longer reflects the artefact's Functional Exposure. 10.2. Where reassessment produces a higher tier: (a) the higher tier shall apply immediately; (b) processing, sharing or deployment shall be suspended where the required safeguards are absent; (c) Annexures 1 and 2 shall be updated where applicable; (d) the MDTAA Clause Selection Tool shall be reapplied; and (e) the relevant Schedules and contractual modules shall be amended.

2.6. Flow-down of obligations

Where a recipient may involve another institution, subprocessor, repository, cloud provider or contractor, equivalent contractual obligations shall be imposed on the downstream recipient.

2.7. Consistency across documents

The MDTAA, its Schedules, any applicable Standard Contractual Clauses, repository terms, project protocols and other agreements shall be interpreted and completed consistently.

Any conflict shall be identified and resolved before signature.

Interpretive note: Selection of an MDTAA module does not establish that the underlying processing or transfer is lawful or that the resulting agreement is enforceable in every jurisdiction. Applicable mandatory law and authorised legal, regulatory, ethics, institutional and repository determinations continue to govern.

1.Compile and record

Compile the Baseline Governance Module and all additional modules selected. Record each selection, its trigger, the responsible party and the provisions implementing it. Complete the relevant schedules, annexures and project-specific fields.

2. Check consistency

Check the selected provisions against Tables 6-8 and other applicable instruments. Resolve conflicting permissions or restrictions, particularly between Steps 8-9, 10-11 and 15-16. Return to the relevant assessment or selection step where clarification is required.

3. Review and finalize

Obtain required legal, ethics, institutional, repository or regulatory review. Do not finalise or execute the MDTAA while mandatory review or another prerequisite remains unresolved. Record the approved agreement version and outstanding implementation conditions.

4, Implement and reassess

Do not commence the relevant activity until required approvals and safeguards are in place. Reapply the affected assessments and module-selection steps when material changes alter the object, tier, purpose, recipients, jurisdictions, infrastructure, access arrangements or required safeguards.

5. CONTRACTUAL MODULES

The Baseline Governance Module applies to every MDTAA. Each additional module applies only where activated through the MDTAA Clause Selection Tool and identified in the Record of Module Selection. Activated modules form binding terms of the executed MDTAA.

5.1. Baseline Governance Module

The Parties shall identify the participating entities, authorised representatives, approved purpose, Neurodata and Governed Artefacts, lawful authority, required approvals, confidentiality obligations, security measures, access limitations, retention arrangements, audit rights, liability, suspension, termination, governing law and dispute-resolution arrangements.

5.2. Cross-Border Transfer Module

The Parties shall record the exporting, receiving, hosting and remotely accessing jurisdictions; the transfer mechanism; destination-law assessment; required approvals; government-access risks; onward-transfer restrictions; and supplementary safeguards.

5.3. Supplementary Safeguards Module

Every safeguard identified through the Neuro-TADT shall be recorded together with the responsible Party, implementation deadline, verification method and consequence of non-implementation. The relevant activity shall not commence until all safeguards identified as conditions precedent have been implemented and verified.

5.4. Enhanced Neurodata Protection Module

The Parties shall implement the safeguards applicable to Tier 3, Tier 4 or Tier 5, as assigned under Annexure 1. Tier 5 obligations apply only to model-associated or computationally persistent artefacts with continuing Functional Exposure.

5.5. Derivative Neurodata Module

The Parties shall specify the authorised transformation, resulting artefacts, provenance, ownership or stewardship, permitted uses, prohibited uses, access conditions, onward transformation, retention, deletion and circumstances requiring reassessment.

5.6. AI and Model Governance Module

The Parties shall specify permitted training, fine-tuning, validation, benchmarking, querying and deployment; prohibited general-purpose or unrelated use; model provenance and versioning; hosting providers; access and output controls; memorisation, extraction, inversion and membership-inference testing; model retention; decommissioning; and technically feasible deletion or unlearning.

5.7. Controlled Access, Repository and Infrastructure Module

The Parties shall identify the repository or technical environment, administrators, providers and subprocessors; permitted access mode; user-authentication requirements; role-based access; query and output restrictions; download controls; storage and processing locations; logging; monitoring; audit; and termination of access.

5.8. Onward Transfer and Subprocessor Module

No onward transfer or subprocessing may occur without the approval specified in this Agreement. Every downstream recipient shall be identified and bound by safeguards no less protective than those required for the assigned tier. The original recipient remains responsible for monitoring compliance and terminating unauthorised access.

5.9. No Onward Transfer Module

The recipient shall not disclose, sublicense, subcontract, replicate, redeposit or otherwise make the Neurodata or Governed Artefact available to another person or entity without prior written approval and completion of any required reassessment.

5.10. Commercial Use and Intellectual Property Module

The Parties shall define permitted and prohibited commercial activities; ownership of background and foreground intellectual property; licensing; publication; confidentiality; commercial development; participant and community interests; benefit allocation; and restrictions on employment, insurance, marketing or discriminatory use.

5.11. Research Use Only Module

Processing shall be restricted to the approved non-commercial research purpose, authorised users, approved methods, approved duration and permitted outputs. Commercial development, unrelated secondary use and deployment outside the approved research context are prohibited unless separately authorised.

5.12. Dataset Linkage Module

The Parties shall identify the datasets authorised for linkage, the linkage purpose, responsible Party, linkage-key governance, access restrictions, prohibited linkages and reassessment requirements. Annexure 1 shall be reapplied before linkage, after which any affected transfer or access pathway shall be reconsidered under Annexure 2.

5.13. Permitted Inference and Prohibited Use Module

The Parties shall identify scientifically approved inferences and expressly prohibit unauthorised reconstruction, profiling, behavioural manipulation, employment or insurance assessment, commercial scoring, law-enforcement use and individual-level decision-making unless specifically lawful and approved.

5.14. Enhanced Audit and Monitoring Module

The Parties shall define access and activity logging, compliance reporting, model-version monitoring, incident notification, inspection rights, testing, independent audit where appropriate, audit frequency, corrective action, suspension and termination.

5.15. Return, Deletion and Certification Module

The Parties shall define deletion or return triggers, deadlines, backup and archival treatment, repository copies, derivative artefacts, permitted legal exceptions, verification evidence and written certification.

5.16. Persistent Artefact, Model Retention and Unlearning Module

Where complete deletion is unavailable, the Parties shall address residual model or embedding persistence, access withdrawal, continued purpose limitation, model isolation, version retirement, decommissioning, source-data deletion, technically feasible unlearning, continuing monitoring and the duration of residual governance obligations.

5.17. Community, Collective and Indigenous Data Governance Module

The Parties shall record applicable community approvals, collective governance conditions, Indigenous data-sovereignty principles, cultural protocols, local governance authority, community-facing accountability, access restrictions and continuing authority over approved secondary use.

5.18. Benefit Sharing and Capacity Development Module 6.3. Review

The completed MDTAA shall be submitted for any required:

6.4. Resolve outstanding issues

Where module selection reveals a governance conflict or unresolved risk, the Parties shall return to the applicable preceding decision tool: (a) Annexure 1 where the Risk Tier or Functional Exposure is uncertain; (b) Annexure 2 where the transfer or access pathway is unsuitable; or (c) Annexure 3 where the governance status of a derivative, embedding or AI system is unresolved.

6.5. Signature

The MDTAA may be signed only when: (a) all required modules have been activated; b) all Schedules and Annexures have been completed; (c) all supplementary safeguards have been implemented or made binding conditions precedent; (d) all governance conflicts have been resolved; (e) all required approvals have been obtained; and (f) the Parties are satisfied that the arrangement preserves Continuity of Protection.

The Clause Selection Tool shall be repeated or updated where: (a) the Risk Tier changes; (b) a new recipient or subprocessor is introduced; (c) the destination jurisdiction changes; (d) the access model changes; (e) a downloadable copy is introduced; (f) a repository, cloud provider or technical environment changes; (g) derivative Neurodata are generated; (h) AI or machine-learning use is introduced or expanded; (i) the approved purpose changes; (j) commercial use is introduced; (k) onward sharing becomes permissible; (l) a new dataset linkage is proposed; (m) deletion becomes technically unavailable; (n) new community or institutional requirements apply; or (o) a material security, legal or governance issue arises. 8.2. 2. Scope

These standards apply whenever Neurodata or a Governed Artefact is: • deposited in a repository; • stored in cloud infrastructure; • accessed remotely; • analysed through a Trusted Research Environment; • accessed through federated analysis; • accessed through secure enclaves; • processed by external vendors; • processed through AI platforms; • shared with external collaborators.

3. Core Principles

The repository or computational environment should ensure:

3.1 Controlled Access

Only authorised users may access Neurodata.

Access shall be proportionate to the assigned Neurodata Risk Tier.

289 3.

For controlled-or limited-access arrangements, only authorised users may access Neurodata. Where public release has been approved under Annexure 1 §3.2 and Annexure 2 Step 8B, the documented release conditions and applicable release-specific safeguards govern access.

3.2 Least Privilege

Users receive only the permissions required for their approved role.

3.3 Purpose Limitation

Access shall be limited to the approved scientific purpose.

Secondary use requires reassessment under Annexures 1-4.

3.4 Continuity of Protection

Protection shall remain equivalent throughout:

3.5 Accountability

Every access decision shall be attributable to an identifiable individual or governance body.

4.6. Federated Analysis

10. Relationship with the MDTAA

Where Annexure 4 activates the: • Repository Module; • Controlled Access Module; • Cloud Module; • Federated Analysis Module; • AI Governance Module; the standards contained in this Annexure shall be deemed incorporated into the MDTAA and shall apply to the extent relevant to the approved governance arrangement.

Figure 1 |

Figure 1 | Six-layer governance framework for comparative neurodata lifecycle analysis. The framework follows neurodata governance from conceptual recognition, through legal conditions for processing and transfer, to the operational arrangements that sustain protection. Layer 1 (Definition & Scope) establishes what counts as neurodata and the boundaries of application. Layer 2 (Lawful Bases & Processing) identifies the legal grounds and purposes that authorize processing. Layer 3 (Cross-Border Transfer & Access) examines the conditions governing the movement of neurodata across jurisdictions and access pathways. Layer 4 (Safeguards & Oversight) identifies the institutional and oversight bodies, together with the technical measures, that protect neurodata. Layer 5 (Enforcement & Remedies) addresses mechanisms for ensuring compliance and responding to violations. Layer 6 (Contractual Clauses & Governance) shows how contractual instruments allocate responsibilities and preserve governance obligations across repositories, institutions and computational infrastructures, providing the basis for our proposed Modular Neurodata Transfer and Access Agreement (MDTAA). Together, the layers show how continuity of protection depends on linked legal, institutional, technical, and contractual conditions throughout the data-to-model lifecycle.

North American results reflect operative governance units rather than sovereign-state jurisdictions (Supplementary Figure 1). Panels correspond to: a. Layer 1: Definition & scope, showing how neurodata are classified under existing legal categories; b. Layer 2: Lawful bases & processing, showing the legal grounds and contexts for processing; c. Layer 3: Cross-border transfer & access, showing the conditions for transfer and access pathways; d. Layer 4: Safeguards & oversight, showing the presence of institutional and technical safeguards; e. Layer 5: Enforcement & remedies, showing compliance, enforcement, and redress mechanisms; and f. Layer 6: Contractual clauses & governance, showing the forms of governance identified. Coloured indicators beneath each panel correspond to the variables defined in the coding instrument (Supplementary Table1).

10.1.

Lawful Basis for Processing and Transfer 10.1.1. The Data Exporter shall ensure that all Personal Data and Neurodata transferred under this Agreement is processed on at least one lawful basis under Articles 6 and 9 of the GDPR and any equivalent legal provisions in other applicable jurisdictions.

11.3.

Relationship With Other MDTA Provisions and Neuro-Specific Rights 11.3.1. The obligations in Clause 10 above shall apply in addition to any further rights afforded to Data Subjects under this Agreement, including neuro-specific protections relating to mental privacy, non-inference, autonomy, and protection against harmful or manipulative automated decision-making.11.3.2. Where this Agreement provides additional or stricter protections for Data Subjects (for example, restrictions on inferring mental states from neurodata), those protections shall apply without limiting or reducing any rights or remedies available to Data Subjects under Clause 10 of the SCCs.11.3.3. In the event of any conflict between the provisions of this Agreement and the verbatim text of Clause 10 above, Clause 10 of the SCCs shall prevail to the extent necessary to ensure an essentially equivalent level of protection for Data Subjects as required under Regulation (EU) 2016/679.

11B. 1.

Where consent is withdrawn or erasure is requested, the Parties shall determine the consequences under Applicable Law, the consent conditions, ethics approval and the approved research protocol. 11B.2. Where deletion is legally or contractually required, the responsible Party shall identify and address: (a) source Neurodata; (b) active and backup copies; (c) derivative features, embeddings, labels and annotations; (d) repository and cloud copies; (e) model-associated artefacts; and (f) onward recipients and subprocessors. 11B.3. Where Neurodata have contributed to a trained model or persistent computational artefact, the responsible Party shall assess whether deletion, retraining, model adjustment or unlearning is technically feasible and proportionate.

12.3.

Transfer Impact Assessments (TIAs) 12.3.1. The assessment referenced in Clause 14(b) shall constitute the Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) for the purposes of this Agreement. The TIA shall be completed by the Data Exporter prior to any transfer and refreshed at least annually or upon material change. 12.3.2. The TIA must specifically evaluate: (a) neurodata sensitivity and inference risks; (b) risk of compelled disclosure by local authorities; (c) encryption and key management safeguards; (d) the feasibility of implementing supplemental measures including encryption, pseudonymisation, data minimisation, secure computing environments, zero-trust architecture, or federated learning. 12.4. Suspension and Termination of Transfers 12.4.1. If the conditions in Clause 14(a)-(f) are not met, the Data Exporter must: • suspend the transfer, and • implement additional safeguards or terminate the relevant portion of the Agreement. 12.4.2. Termination and post-termination duties shall follow Clause 16(d) and (e) SCC and Article 15 of this MDTA.

Tier 5 -Model-associated or computationally persistent neurodata with continuing functional exposure Description Tier 5 applies where Neurodata-derived information is associated with an AI model or persistent computational infrastructure and the particular artefact retains, or may reasonably retain, continuing Functional Exposure through inference, reconstruction, extraction, profiling, memorisation, prediction or another consequential use. Where model incorporation is known but continuing exposure cannot be determined, the artefact shall receive a provisional classification pending assessment under Annexure 3 and appropriate specialist review. Examples (a) model weights trained using Neurodata; (b) neuroscience foundation models; (c) federated-learning systems; (d) synthetic-data generators trained on Neurodata; (e) persistent embedding repositories; (a) specialist AI and model-governance review; (b) documentation of model provenance, training data and authorised purposes; (c) identification of hosting providers, cloud providers and subprocessors; (d) assessment of inversion, extraction and memorisation risks; (e) restrictions on copying, retraining, fine-tuning, redistribution and onward use; (f) controls governing model access, deployment and output generation; (g) auditability and continuing monitoring; (h) defined retention, deletion and, where technically feasible, model-unlearning procedures; (i) completion of the Derivative and Embedding Governance Decision Tool; and (j) completion or reassessment of the Transfer and Access Decision Tool before any external access, transfer or deployment.

12. CONTINUING COMPLIANCE 12.1. Approval under this Annexure is conditional on continuing compliance with: (a) Applicable Law; (b) participant consent and lawful-processing conditions; (c) ethics and institutional approvals; (d) repository and infrastructure requirements; (e) Annexures 1 and 2; (f) the MDTAA; and (g) all restrictions recorded in the completed assessment.12.2. Approval may be suspended or withdrawn where: (a) the transformed output demonstrates previously unknown capabilities; (b) unauthorised inference, reconstruction, linkage or profiling becomes possible; (c) model memorisation, inversion or extraction risk materially increases; (d) the artefact is used for an unauthorised purpose; (e) an unapproved recipient obtains access; (f) the artefact is retrained, fine-tuned or redistributed without approval; (g) required safeguards cease to operate effectively; or (h) the responsible Party can no longer demonstrate Continuity of Protection. This Annexure establishes the MDTAA Clause Selection Tool applicable under the Modular Neurodata Transfer and Access Agreement ("MDTAA"). The purpose of this Annexure is to translate the governance decisions generated through Annexures 1-3 into the contractual modules, clauses, Schedules and safeguards required for the proposed Neurodata transfer, access, transformation, reuse or AI-enabled processing arrangement. The MDTAA Clause Selection Tool shall be completed after: (a) classification of the relevant Neurodata or Governed Artefact under the Neurodata Governance Decision Tool in Annexure 1; (b) assessment of any proposed external, repository, remote or cross-border access pathway under the Neurodata Transfer and Access Decision Tool in Annexure 2; and (c) assessment of any derivative Neurodata, transformed representation or AI-enabled processing under the Neural Derivative and Embedding Governance Decision Tool in Annexure 3. This Annexure does not itself draft or replace the substantive terms of the MDTAA. It identifies which contractual modules shall be activated, completed or strengthened in light of the governance characteristics identified through the preceding decision tools.The completed MDTAA shall therefore constitute the contractual implementation of the governance workflow rather than a generic transfer agreement applied without regard to the nature of the Neurodata, the proposed transfer pathway or downstream technical use.The MDTAA is intended to complement, and not replace: (a) Applicable Law; (b) ethics approvals and institutional approvals; (c) participant consent and lawful-processing requirements; (d) repository terms and access conditions; (e) Data Transfer Agreements, Data Use Agreements and institutional agreements; (f) Standard Contractual Clauses, model clauses or other mandatory transfer mechanisms; (g) regulatory authorisations; and (h) any other binding legal, contractual, funder or governance requirement.

8.4 . Accuracy 10 . 1 . 2.

The lawful basis relied upon must be clearly recorded in Schedule B, including any special-category justifications for processing Neurodata, genetic data, mental-health data, or biometric identifiers. 10.1.3. The lawful basis must be compatible with the requirements of SCC Clause 8.1 (purpose limitation) and must enable the Data Importer to comply with the transparency and accuracy obligations in SCC Clause 8.2 and 8.3.10.2. Consent Requirements 10.2.1. Where consent is used as the lawful basis, the consent must meet the requirements of GDPR Articles 4(11), 7 and 9, as well as SCC Clause 8.1(i) (data subject consent for secondary purposes).

10.2 . 2.

Consent must be: (a) specific, informed, freely given, and unambiguous; (b) capable of being withdrawn at any time; (c) documented and auditable; (d) consistent with the Data Subject Rights obligations contained in Article 11 and SCC Clause 10.10.2.3. Where appropriate, consent may be managed through dynamic or digital consent mechanisms, as described as described in applicable project documentation, ethics approvals, or Schedule B, provided that: (a) withdrawal of consent triggers erasure or restrictions under SCC Clause 10(b)(iii); (b) the Data Importer is notified without undue delay; (c) the Data Importer does not continue processing beyond the limits of the withdrawn consent. 10.3. Withdrawal of Consent 10.3.1. Where consent is withdrawn, the Data Exporter shall notify the Data Importer without undue delay and ensure cessation of any processing incompatible with the withdrawal. 10.3.2. Upon withdrawal, the Data Importer shall: (a) erase or restrict processing of the relevant Personal Data in accordance with SCC Clause 10(b)(iii); (b) ensure all authorised sub-processors comply with the withdrawal; (c) provide confirmation to the Data Exporter of completion of actions taken. 10.3.3. Withdrawal applies prospectively and does not retroactively invalidate previously lawful processing activities. 10.4. Transparency and Notice Obligations 10.4.1. The Data Exporter shall provide Data Subjects with all notice required under GDPR Articles 13-14 and SCC Clause 8.2(d). 10.4.2. Any consent notice, privacy notice or research participant information sheet must contain clear explanations of Data Subject Rights set out in: (a) Article 11 of this Agreement, and (b) SCC Clause 10 (verbatim text) incorporated into Article 11.10.4.3. The notices must inform Data Subjects, in clear and plain language, of their right to: supervisory authorities. These requirements directly reflect SCC Clause 10(a)-(d).

10.5.

Alignment with SCC Clause 10 (Data Subject Rights) 10.5.1. All consent-related procedures under this Article must be implemented in a manner that enables Data Subjects to exercise their rights under Article 11 of this Agreement. 10.5.2. Where Data Subjects submit requests relating to their consent or the lawfulness of processing, the Data Importer shall comply with its obligations under: (a) SCC Clause 10(a) (time limits & accessibility); (b) Clause 10(b) (confirmation, copies, rectification, erasure); (c) Clause 10(d) (automated decision safeguards); (d) Clause 10(e)-(g) (fees, refusals, and justifications).

10.5 . 3 . 1.

In case of conflict between this Article and the SCCs, SCC Clause 10 prevails as required by Article 3. Where Neurodata is collected on the basis of consent, the Data Exporter must ensure that Data Subjects are informed about:(a) the potential inferential power of the Neurodata;(b) any risk of automated or algorithmic profiling;(c) any possibility of downstream machine-learning training or model development. 10.6.2. This Annexure establishes the Neurodata Transfer and Access Decision Tool ("Neuro-TADT") applicable under the Modular Neurodata Transfer and Access Agreement ("MDTAA").1.2. The Neuro-TADT enables the Parties, researchers, repository managers, Data Access Committees, ethics committees, data stewards and other authorised governance bodies to determine whether a proposed transfer or access pathway can preserve the level of protection required by the Neurodata Risk Tier assigned under Annexure 1. The Neuro-TADT applies where Neurodata or a Governed Artefact is proposed to be: (a) shared with another institution or research collaborator; (b) transferred across national or jurisdictional borders; (c) deposited in or accessed through a repository; (d) accessed remotely through a secure research environment; (e) hosted or processed in a cloud-computing environment; (f) made accessible to a commercial partner, vendor or AI developer; (g) processed through federated, query-only or distributed computational infrastructure; or (h) otherwise made accessible outside the originating Party's internal governance environment. The Neuro-TADT shall be completed only after the relevant Neurodata or Governed Artefact has been assessed and assigned a Neurodata Risk Tier under the Neurodata Governance Decision Tool in Annexure 1. The Neuro-TADT assesses the proposed transfer or access pathway, rather than reclassifying the Neurodata object itself.
